articles.title: A regulatory fix for India’s campuses
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The Ministry must act without delay and issue a statutory notification, consistent with the court’s judgment, for eligible educational campuses

India’s education infrastructure has always been the strongest foundation of its growth and development. However, recent Supreme Court judgments have reaffirmed that educational buildings exceeding 20,000 square metres require prior Environmental Clearance (EC) under the Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) Notification, 2006. Institutions that have already constructed such buildings without obtaining clearance are now left without any procedure to secure it, creating a serious obstacle. The issue has developed because of two major regulatory changes.

Before the EIA Notification, 2006, there was no built-up-area-based EC requirement for educational institutions. The Notification brought large construction projects, including educational campuses, within the prior EC framework. In December 2014, the Union government exempted schools, colleges and institutional hostels from EC, subject to environmental management conditions. The Kerala High Court quashed this exemption in March 2024. The government introduced a fresh exemption in January 2025, but Vanashakti challenged it before the Supreme Court. After staying its operation, the court cancelled the exemption in August 2025. Consequently, large educational buildings again became subject to prior EC requirements.
Science, Space & Environment Report: A regulatory fix for India’s campuses. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

Scientific & Technical Core: Innovations led by ISRO, DRDO, CSIR, and national research institutes are advancing India's capabilities in space exploration, quantum computing, biotechnology, and clean energy.

articles.title: UEF, IIT-M join hands for Tamil Nadu Growth Conclave 2026; focus on 10 key sectors
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The United Economic Forum (UEF) Chamber of Commerce has signed an MoU with the Indian Institute of Technology - Madras (IIT-M) to collaborate for the Tamil Nadu Growth Conclave 2026 scheduled to be held on December 8, 2026. The objective of this MoU is to facilitate knowledge sharing, industry academia collaboration, innovation, investment and stakeholder engagement towards Tamil Nadu’s economic growth.

The event will focus on 10 sectors, including Automotive & EV; Electronics & Semiconductors; IT, AI and Digital; Advanced Engineering & Capital Goods; Textiles & Technical Textiles; Pharma, Biotech & MedTech; Agri & Food Processing; Renewable & Green Energy; Logistics, Ports & Global Trade and Aerospace & Defence. Professors from the IIT-M ecosystem will lead each of these sectors.

V.Kamakoti, IIT-Madras Director through a video message said: “IIT Madras, and IIT Madras Research Park, and all our ecosystem are very happy to be associated with UEF to launch this Tamil Nadu Conclave 2026 as we march towards a multi-trillion economy.”

Mr. Kamakoti further said: “There are 10 highly emerging and extremely important from a societal angle verticals that have been identified, all the way from automotive, EV, electronics, semiconductor, IT, AI, technical, textiles, pharma, agri, renewable, green energy, aerospace, defense, logistics, and advanced engineering and capital goods.” He added, “And in each of these verticals, we are going to talk not just about the products, but also the supply chain, the logistics that is involved, the raw materials that are involved to make these, because many of them are deep tech technologies.”

Jinnah Rafiq Ahmed, Chairman, UEF – Tamil Nadu Growth Conclave 2026 and Executive Chairman and Managing Director, Kothari Industrial Corporation Limited (KICL), said that a few MoUs would be inked at the conclave. To a query on whether investments are moving out of Tamil Nadu, he said that a lot of companies want to come to Tamil Nadu.

“Tamil Nadu’s industrial growth will be there, will continue and it will be unimaginable. Definitely, Tamil Nadu’s industrial growth will be very aggressive in the coming years. An industry from Tamil Nadu going out of State will not happen. And if it is, it might be an additional project in other States,” he said.

Ahmed A. R. Buhari, President — United Economic Forum (UEF) said, “Tamil Nadu has set an ambitious target of becoming a $1.5 trillion economy by 2036. UEF’s Unnatha Tamizhagam vision aspires to contribute towards Tamil Nadu becoming a $4 trillion economy by 2047.” The United Economic Forum in association with Kothari Industrial Corporation Limited and Airtel Business is organising the Tamil Nadu Growth Conclave 2026.

articles.title: Armed robbers loot jewellery worth more than ₹30 crore at gunpoint in Bihar’s Bettiah
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: According to the police, eight robbers arrived at the jewellery shop on three motorcycles and seized the mobile phone and then tied their hands.
Armed robbers looted jewellery worth more than ₹30 crore at gunpoint on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) in broad daylight in Bettiah, the district headquarters of West Champaran, Bihar.

The loot is seen as one of the biggest heists in recent times. According to the police, eight robbers arrived at the jewellery showroom on three motorcycles, seized mobile phones, and then tied the hands of the victims.

The robber also hit two staff members, including a security guard, with a gun, leaving them injured. A woman staff member, while speaking to local media, said that before leaving the showroom with the looted jewellery, one robber said, “This is just the trailer; the film is yet to come. We will return.”

The owner of the jewellery showroom is Brajesh Kushwaha, a leader of the ruling Janata Dal (United). The incident took place at Senco Gold and Diamonds, located near Supriya Cinema Road, under the jurisdiction of Kali Bagh police station.
Former Deputy Chief Minister and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Renu Devi, whose residence is close to the showroom, also visited the place, calling it the first major robbery in Bettiah.

Bettiah, Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Harkishore Rai, and Superintendent of Police (SP) Kumar Gautam also went to the spot and questioned the staff. According to Mr. Rai, the police have constituted special teams to identify and arrest the accused. The exact value of the stolen jewellery is yet to be assessed.

“Police are investigating the case, and we have launched extensive raids to arrest the culprits. We have also obtained CCTV footage in which the robbers are visible. Based on the CCTV footage and other evidence, the police will surely catch them and recover the looted jewellery,” said a senior police official.

articles.title: NIA arrests Khalistan Zindabad Force ‘supporter’ deported from U.S. in Rajpura-Shambhu blast case

The National Investigation Agency (NIA) on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) arrested Surinder Singh, an alleged supporter of the banned terror outfit Khalistan Zindabad Force (KZF), at Delhi airport following his deportation by U.S. authorities.

He was arrested in connection with the blast on the railway line of the Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL), between Shambhu and Rajpura stations, on April 27. “The blast was carried out to further the terror activities of the KZF, disrupt communal harmony, and destabilise law and order in Punjab,” the agency said.

He described the KZF as a “ Qaumi Organisation” and referred to designated individual terrorist Ranjeet Singh alias Neeta as “the general of the Qaum ”, the agency alleged.
The NIA had issued a Look Out Circular (LOC) against Surinder Singh during the investigation. Multiple criminal cases are also registered against him in different districts of Punjab.

“With this arrest, the NIA has so far arrested eight accused in the Rajpura-Shambhu blast case. The agency’s investigation into the wider conspiracy continues, including efforts to dismantle the nexus between terrorists and their associates based abroad and break their funding networks and infrastructure,” the agency said.

articles.title: Plea in Supreme Court asks how many voters have refilled enumeration forms to get back on electoral rolls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Petitioners seek disclosure of the number of ASDD voters who have submitted enumeration forms and want those who used Form 6 to retain their old EPIC numbers

A fresh petition has been filed in the Supreme Court seeking disclosure of the number of Delhi voters whose names were deleted from the draft electoral rolls under the absent, shifted, dead and duplicate (ASDD) categories but who subsequently submitted enumeration forms to be restored to the voter list.
The petitioners have also sought an extension of the provision allowing such voters to submit enumeration forms and the restoration of their old Electoral Photo Identity Card (EPIC) numbers.

Filed on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) by transparency rights activists Anjali Bharadwaj and Amrita Johri, the petition argues that ASDD voters who have already submitted Form 6 should also be allowed to fill enumeration forms.

This, they said, would ensure that they are restored to the electoral rolls with their existing EPIC numbers instead of being classified as new voters. Form 6 is intended for registering new voters but had also been used by those whose names were deleted during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).

During an earlier hearing, the Supreme Court had termed the use of Form 6 by voters excluded from the draft rolls under the ASDD category an “error”, as the form requires applicants to declare that they are first-time voters.

Subsequently, the Election Commission of India issued a directive allowing voters marked as ASDD in seven States, including Delhi, where the SIR is under way, to submit enumeration forms again instead of using Form 6. These voters had been excluded because their issued enumeration forms were not received back.
The petition has also raised concerns over the alleged misuse of Form 7 for targeted deletions. It has sought an audit and public disclosure of all Form 7 applications submitted so far.

The petitioners have further requested that booth-level agents (BLAs) of political parties filing Form 7 be required to identify themselves as party representatives rather than submitting applications only under their individual names.

articles.title: U.S., Venezuela sign deal to re-establish military ties: Hegseth
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The U.S. Defence Secretary said that following the January capture of Nicolas Maduro by the U.S. military, the country “has gone from our most aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner”
Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, speaking in Venezuela, said the two countries have signed an agreement to re-establish military ties, from training to intelligence sharing.

Mr. Hegseth said that following the January capture of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro by the U.S. military, the country “has gone from our most aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner.”
Mr. Hegseth also praised the “close cooperation” with interim President Delcy Rodriguez that allowed officials “to stabilise Venezuela and rid it of narco-terrorists once and for all.”
The Pentagon did not immediately offer further details on the new partnership.

Ms. Rodríguez separately lauded the opportunity to strengthen the military partnership. “I hope that this technical-military cooperation … can be brought to its highest possible level so that ... we may address common threats,” she said.
Mr. Hegseth’s visit underscores efforts by President Donald Trump’s administration to deepen its influence in the South American country since U.S. forces ousted Maduro in January.

Mr. Hegseth is the latest member of Mr. Trump’s Cabinet to travel to Venezuela following visits this year by the Interior and Energy secretaries, who have focused on efforts to tap its oil reserves and critical minerals. Mr. Trump said in August that Mr. Hegseth helped broker a sweeping deal for the U.S. to take control of some Venezuelan oil reserves.
The head of U.S. military operations in Latin America, Gen. Francis Donovan of U.S. Southern Command, also has met interim authorities in Venezuela at least twice this year.

The U.S. military has been expanding its attention on the region since Mr. Trump returned to the White House last year, with the Republican president promising to focus more on the Western Hemisphere and battle Latin American drug cartels.

To try to stem the flow of narcotics into the U.S. and the scourge of fatal overdoses, American forces have been attacking what the Trump administration says are boats smuggling drugs in the Caribbean Sea and the eastern Pacific Ocean. At least 240 people have been killed since the administration began targeting those it calls “narcoterrorists” in September 2025, although U.S. officials have released little evidence publicly to support claims the vessels were carrying drugs.

Mr. Hegseth’s visit comes at a time of uncertainty for Venezuelans regarding who will lead the nation in the coming months and years. Ms. Rodríguez, a Maduro ally, took over in Venezuela after Mr. Maduro’s capture. Ms. Rodríguez’s court-allowed term expired in July, but she continues to function as Venezuela’s head of state.
Opposition leader María Corina Machado recently returned to Venezuela from exile following seven failed attempts that opposition activists claimed were thwarted by the government.

articles.title: Panjab University improves its global standing in interdisciplinary scientific research
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The 2027 edition of the rankings, produced by Times Higher Education in association with Schmidt Science Fellows, assessed 1,058 institutions across 102 countries and territories, compared with 911 institutions in the 2026 edition

Chandigarh-based Panjab University (PU) has improved its global standing in interdisciplinary scientific research, climbing 24 places to secure the joint 150th position in the Times Higher Education (THE) Interdisciplinary Science Rankings 2027. The University’s overall score has increased to 55.0 from 52.8 in 2026 and 48.6 in 2025.

In a statement on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), Vice-Chancellor Meenakshi Goyal said, “This improvement in Panjab University’s global standing reflects our continued commitment to strengthening interdisciplinary research and academic collaboration. It is the outcome of the collective efforts of our faculty, researchers, students, and staff. We will continue to build an enabling research ecosystem that encourages collaboration across disciplines, supports innovation, and addresses complex societal challenges aimed at Viksit Bharat through knowledge and research.”

The 2027 edition of the rankings, produced by Times Higher Education in association with Schmidt Science Fellows, assessed 1,058 institutions across 102 countries and territories, compared with 911 institutions in the 2026 edition. A total of 565 Asian institutions were ranked, up from 478 last year.

The Interdisciplinary Science Rankings assess universities’ contributions and commitment to research that brings together knowledge and methods from different academic disciplines to address complex challenges. The rankings cover collaborations involving multiple scientific disciplines as well as research combining scientific disciplines with areas such as the social sciences, education, psychology, law, economics, and clinical and health studies.

articles.title: Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University in Andhra Pradesh gets ‘A’ grade from ICAR
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: This accreditation grade is valid from March 2026 to March 2031

Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU) has secured ‘A’ grade accreditation from the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), marking a significant improvement in its national standing.
The university, which previously held a B grade, achieved the higher rating following improvements in education, research and agricultural extension activities.

Vice-Chancellor P.V. Satyanarayana told the media on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) that the accreditation was valid from March 2026 to March 2031. A national-level peer review team assessed the university’s academic standards, research work, quality of education and efforts to provide modern agricultural technologies to farmers before awarding the ‘A’ grade.
The recognition is expected to enhance the university’s national reputation, create better opportunities for students in higher education and research, and help it secure more national-level funding.

He credited the achievement to the collective efforts of former Vice-Chancellors, scientists, university officials, teaching and non-teaching staff, associate deans and associate directors of research.

fullParagraphs: Communist Party of India (Marxist) State Secretariat member P. Jayarajan has alleged that the Ariyil Shukkoor case was a political hatchet job orchestrated by the then ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) and the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) leadership with the help of the Kerala Police to target the CPI(M).

He was speaking to reporters outside the SBI Special Court here on Thursday (November 19, 2026) after Special Judge P. Sabarinathan acquitted him, former Kalliasseri MLA T.V. Rajesh and 16 others in the case.

Mr. Jayarajan alleged that invoking IPC Section 118 (concealing a design to commit an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life) was part of a conspiracy theory. “Although Comrade Rajesh and I were lying injured in hospital, the Kerala Police charged us under Section 118. To support this allegation, they arraigned in two League sympathisers as witnesses. The police fabricated a case claiming that a conspiracy had been hatched inside the hospital room,” he alleged.

After taking over the investigation, the CBI added IPC Section 120 and developed a fresh conspiracy narrative. Five witnesses were cited in support of this theory. Instead of correcting the politically motivated course adopted by the Kerala Police, the central investigating agency effectively reinforced it, he alleged.

He claimed that a major reason why the court acquitted comrade Rajesh and me was that certain individuals within the IUML were unwilling to stand by fabricated testimony. The League leadership, which made disgraceful attempts to drag us into this conspiracy case, owes an apology to the people. So do the leaders of the then UDF government, he said.

Mr. Rajesh alleged that the conspiracy theory, the “party court” narrative, and similar allegations were deliberately fabricated with the conscious aim of undermining the influence the CPI(M) had gained among minority communities. The propaganda campaign began just before the Neyyattinkara by-election, a UDF stronghold. It was carefully planned and executed by the UDF leadership, he alleged.

He said that in a complaint filed before the Taliparamba Magistrate Court in connection with the case, the two League sympathisers cited as witnesses by the police had stated in sworn affidavits that they had never visited CPI(M) leaders in the hospital room. “False witnesses were created by the police to place Comrade Jayarajan, myself and the party in the dock, and to wage a large-scale misinformation campaign against the CPI(M). The League minister who made certain statements regarding the witnesses must explain why those witnesses could not ultimately be produced,” he alleged.

Those who attempted to tarnish the image of the CPI(M) must now accept responsibility. The Muslim League leadership, the Congress leadership of that period, and the then Home Minister should publicly apologise, Mr. Rajesh said.

articles.title: Tolichowki Police Inspector caught taking ₹20,000 bribe to let hotel operate beyond 1 a.m
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tolichowki Police Inspector in Hyderabad was arrested by the Telangana Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) for allegedly demanding and accepting a bribe of ₹20,000 from a representative of a hotel management to extend official favours.

The Inspector L. Ramesh Naik, attached to Tolichowki Police Station under the Golconda Zone of the Hyderabad City Police Commissionerate, was caught red-handed by the ACB officials of City Range-I at around 9.40 p.m. on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) while accepting the bribe amount.

The inspector demanded a total bribe of ₹40,000 from the complainant in exchange for not taking coercive action against the hotel management and allowing its cafeteria to operate beyond 1 a.m. by an additional hour on a monthly basis. The arrangement was intended to facilitate the completion of online food orders.

The ACB said that the inspector had initially demanded a monthly bribe of ₹50,000 on October 31. He accepted ₹20,000 at the time and agreed to reduce the amount by ₹10,000 for the first month, fixing the bribe at ₹40,000. The ₹20,000 accepted on Wednesday was the remaining balance. The tainted amount of ₹20,000 was recovered from the Inspector’s possession at his instance. During the trap, the ACB officials also found him in possession of unaccounted cash amounting to ₹1.80 lakh, kept in four separate envelopes.
He was arrested and produced before the Additional Special Judge for SPE and ACB Cases at Nampally for judicial remand. The case is under investigation.

articles.title: Hyderabad doctor brings down rare disease drug cost from ₹9 crore to ₹2.5 lakh; seven children to get free treatment
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Seven children diagnosed with Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome (AHDS), a rare genetic disorder, are set to receive a year’s supply of the medicine tiratricol free of cost on November 30; the compounded formulation is estimated to cost just ₹2.5 lakh per child for a year

Imagine having a medicine that could help manage your child’s rare genetic condition, but being unable to afford it because a year’s treatment costs as much as ₹9 crore. For seven families in India, that situation could soon change.

Seven children diagnosed with Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome (AHDS), a rare genetic disorder, are set to receive a year’s supply of the medicine tiratricol free of cost on November 30, following an initiative led by Hyderabad-based paediatrician Dr. Sivaranjani Santosh and Access to Medicines India.

The development is significant not just because the families will receive the medicine without paying for it, but also because its cost has been brought down through pharmaceutical compounding in the Netherlands. While the commercial version of the drug costs approximately ₹4.68 crore to ₹9 crore per child annually, the compounded formulation is estimated to cost just ₹2.5 lakh per child for a year.

The medicine has been prepared by Transvaal Pharmacy in The Hague, Netherlands, with support from the Netherlands-based Pharmaceutical Accountability Foundation (PAF). The first batch will be handed over to the parents of the seven children along with the necessary documentation and individual import permissions. The families have secured approvals for one year of treatment. As the compounded medicine has a shelf life of six months, it will be imported in two batches.

The initiative began after Arav, a child under the care of Dr. Sivaranjani, was diagnosed with AHDS, also known as MCT8 deficiency. The condition is caused by mutations affecting the MCT8 gene, which plays an important role in transporting thyroid hormones into brain cells. Tiratricol, also known as TRIAC, acts on thyroid hormone receptors and may help overcome some effects of the deficiency. It also helps minimise complications associated with peripheral thyrotoxicosis.

Although the medicine was available in Europe, its commercial price put it beyond the reach of most Indian families. Arav’s mother, Pavitra Sirolkar, had to arrange approximately ₹12 lakh to ₹13 lakh for just one month’s supply of the medicine from Germany. Dr Sivaranjani initially approached paediatricians, endocrinologists and paediatric neurologists to explore ways of procuring the drug. Doctors at Christian Medical College (CMC), Vellore, where five other children with the same condition had been identified, were also approached.

Attempts to obtain the medicine through pharmaceutical company Egetis Therapeutics and its compassionate-use programme did not succeed. The situation eventually prompted Dr Sivaranjani to take the issue to social media. On September 7, she posted an appeal seeking help for the family and urged people to tag the Prime Minister, Union Health Minister and other government representatives. The appeal gained attention, bringing it to the notice of PAF.

The foundation subsequently explored the possibility of preparing the medicine through pharmaceutical compounding using the active pharmaceutical ingredient. Transvaal Pharmacy conducted test batches and developed a formulation for the seven children. The initial group included Arav and five children receiving treatment at CMC Vellore. A seventh child, aged one year, was identified after his father contacted Dr Sivaranjani following her social media appeal.

According to PAF, the total cost of providing one year’s treatment to all seven children is €14,200, approximately ₹15.08 lakh. Of this, Dr Sivaranjani raised approximately ₹6.09 lakh in India, while PAF undertook to raise the remaining €8,600, approximately ₹9.13 lakh, in the Netherlands. The medicine will be provided to all seven families free of cost.

While the November 30 handover addresses the immediate treatment requirements of the seven children, Dr Sivaranjani believes that importing the medicine cannot be a permanent solution. She plans to approach the Union government and work with Access to Medicines India and other organisations to explore the possibility of getting the medicine compounded in India and making it accessible to more children.

“How can a medicine be available in the world but not be available for our children? We should get the medicine compounded in India and make it available for all the children with this condition,” she said.

fullParagraphs: Since India has already shown the world how to make drugs affordable, the next challenge is to show the world how to make rare-disease drugs accessible; with a streamlined regulatory pathway, appropriate financial incentives, and government procurement, India could build a globally competitive rare-disease pharmaceutical sector

Each rare disease affects very few people. However, there are around 8,000 rare diseases, and they cumulatively affect hundreds of millions of people. In India, 1,004 rare genetic disorders have been reported so far.

It used to be that because the number of patients for a rare-disease drug was very small, so the pharmaceutical industry’s interest in developing such drugs was limited. Therefore they were called orphan drugs.

articles.title: Jewellery traders in Bapatla told to strengthen security at shops
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Jewellery shop owners and pawn brokers told to install advanced CCTV cameras and burglar alarm systems on their premises

Bapatla District Superintendent of Police B. Umamaheswar has directed gold and silver jewellery shop owners and pawn brokers to strengthen security measures on their premises by installing advanced CCTV cameras and burglar alarm systems to prevent thefts.

Addressing a meeting with jewellery traders and pawn brokers at his camp office in Bapatla on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), the SP said the police had identified 257 gold and silver jewellery shops in the district. Recent thefts and the increase in gold prices necessitated enhanced security at commercial establishments, he said.

Mr. Umamaheswar advised shop owners to install high quality CCTV cameras covering interiors, exteriors, counters and strong rooms. They should ensure clear night-time recording through night vision cameras and keep digital video recorders (DVRs) in secure locations. He also stressed the need for burglar alarm systems to detect attempted break-ins.

The SP cautioned traders against purchasing gold or silver ornaments without proper supporting documents. He urged them to immediately inform the police about suspicious persons or activities and coordinate with the department to prevent crimes.
He said the district’s mobile forensic unit was helping in investigations. The police have recently cracked a jewellery theft case in Karlapalem and arrested the accused, he said.

articles.title: Yunus's ancestral home set ablaze as violence grips Bangladesh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Crude bomb explosions rocked Bangladesh's capital before dawn, while former interim government chief Muhammad Yunus's ancestral home was torched in Chattogram. The unrest followed a Thursday (November 19, 2026) "lockdown" call by the banned Awami League, led by former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
Police and witnesses said at least four people were wounded. Witnesses reported explosions of a series of improvised devices, arson attacks and vandalism in Dhaka despite stepped-up security.
Unidentified arsonists set fire to Mr. Yunus's paternal home at Chattogram's Panchlaish area after several branches of his Grameen Bank in different parts of Bangladesh were set on fire.

Newspaper reports said rival activists, presumably belonging to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), overnight attacked or set ablaze the residences of two Awami League leaders in Dhaka.

Police said they stepped up security overnight, mobilising more personnel at major flyovers across the capital. At the same time, officers were seen checking vehicles at entry and exit points and questioning motorcyclists and drivers of suspicious vehicles.

Awami League called the lockdown coinciding with the anniversary of a special tribunal verdict sentencing Ms. Hasina to death last year after trying her in absentia on charges of committing crimes against humanity.

Ms. Hasina, 79, has been living in India since fleeing Bangladesh on August 5, 2024, following a student-led protest called the July Uprising that toppled her government. Bangladesh has been seeking her extradition from India.

Officials said thousands of paramilitary Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) troops were called out to maintain order in sensitive districts including southwestern Gopalganj district, Ms. Hasina's birthplace.

According to BDnews24 , police arrested 565 people in a 24-hour drive in Dhaka alone ahead of the lockdown, with one prominent person being former Education Minister in Ms. Hasina's cabinet Nurul Islam Nahid, who was detained from his Dhaka residence at midnight on Wednesday (November 18, 2026).

Prime Minister Tarique on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) night sought "democratic forces" unity to prevent "resurgence" of Awami League, describing it as a "terrorist outfit" and "fallen, defeated, and ousted fascist force" and called for actions for its "decisive defeat".

"Let us once again unite in the spirit of 2024, when we drove the autocratic forces out of this country, and ensure that those forces are decisively defeated," Mr. Rahman said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) night in a parliamentary address, where BNP's once ally Jamaat-e-Islami is the main opposition party. Ahead of his address at the closing sitting of the current parliamentary session, he met with party lawmakers and asked them to return immediately to their constituencies to maintain a visible presence on the streets.

The Daily Star said Rahman asked BNP lawmakers not to rely solely on government machinery or the administration to counter Awami League activists, but instead to work closely with the party's grassroots leaders and workers.

articles.title: Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral meeting LIVE: Xi says China-U.S. relations 'stable and improved'
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The war in ‌Ukraine dominated a meeting between Russian ​President Vladimir Putin ⁠and U.S. President Donald Trump, Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri ‌Ushakov said on Thursday, November 19

Some in the West are comparing the three-way meeting to the 1945 Yalta conference, where the wartime leaders of the U.S., Britain and the Soviet Union divided Germany and Berlin, carved out zones of influence in Europe, and agreed to establish the United Nations.
The Kremlin, which long has courted the concept of a “multipolar world” offering an equal say to all nations, plays down the Yalta comparisons, which are also unwelcome to China for similar reasons.

Fyodor Lukyanov, a pro-Kremlin foreign policy expert, noted that even as Moscow publicly rejects the Yalta analogy, it seems to believe the leaders could “reach agreements and make decisions that will determine global developments”.
Of the three nations, “it seems that only Russia really believes in the possibility of global control”, he told a recent roundtable.

Chatham House director Bronwen Maddox said in a commentary that “standing with Xi and Trump, Putin will look like one of the three main leaders of the world”, even though “Russia is no superpower” and its economy, overloaded with military spending, is dwindling.
She warned that “the danger for Ukraine is that Trump uses this summit to try to advance his notion of peace, including giving Russia territory it has not managed to seize by force”.

The meeting follows US-mediated peace talks between Russia and Ukraine held in Abu Dhabi last week for the first time in nine months. The negotiations produced few visible results as the parties stuck to their sharply divergent demands. -- AP
Trilateral Xi-Putin-Trump summit draws Yalta 1945 comparisons, highlighting postwar order shifts amid Ukraine tensions and multipolar world debates.
The United States and China want to help end the war in Ukraine, U.S. President Donald Trump said on Thursday (November 19, 2026) as he met his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping in Shenzhen.
“We’re looking to both help with respect to the war with Russia and Ukraine. I’d like to see it ended, I think I can speak for both of us, very much,” Mr. Trump said.

Ukraine struck the bridge linking Russia and ⁠Crimea for the third time in a week, forcing a suspension of train services across it, Russian authorities said, hours before President Vladimir ‌Putin was due to meet the leaders of China and the U.S..

The timing and impact of ‌Ukraine’s attacks on the bridge, the longest in Europe ‌and ⁠a symbol of Putin’s Russia, are awkward for the ⁠Kremlin chief as he prepares to participate in what Moscow has cast as a historic trilateral summit with U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping later ‌on Thursday (November 19, 2026). Moscow hopes the meeting will send a signal to allies and foes that it - and not the European Union and Britain - is part of an emerging new multilateral ‌world order.

articles.title: India, Canada eye defence pact during Modi visit in December
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: India’s High Commissioner to Ottawa says both countries cannot afford to let fringe issues derail their extensive mutual interests
India and Canada could be announcing a defence agreement during Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s official visit in December, according to the country’s High Commissioner to Ottawa, Dinesh K. Patnaik.
Both countries are also in the final stages of negotiations of a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement. “We are on the cusp of finalising it,” Mr. Patnaik said.

Addressing a gathering in the Canadian capital organised by the Centre for Strategic Statecraft and the Canadian International Council, he said that both countries cannot afford to let fringe issues derail their extensive mutual interests.

Mr. Patnaik took over as India’s High Commissioner to Ottawa in September 2025. Both countries had earlier expelled each other’s High Commissioners and reduced their diplomatic presence following the murder of Sikh Khalistani activist Hardeep Singh Nijjar in June 2023. Then Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau accused India of orchestrating the murder, throwing bilateral relations into a tailspin. Subsequent reports by Canadian agencies also listed India, alongside China and Russia, as an interferer in domestic politics. The turnaround in ties, which began with the mutual reinstatement of High Commissioners, is set to reach a milestone with Mr. Modi’s visit on December 11 and 12.

Mr. Patnaik said India and Canada are no longer talking about a reset of their derailed relations, but rather an overarching boost in ties spanning defence, space, nuclear energy, deep tech, trade, and the mobility of people. The two nations have moved from a complete lack of trust over a year ago to an unprecedented degree of mutual trust, he added.

“The fact is that in the core strategic concerns of Canada and India, there is no conflict. Still, all it took for the entire bilateral relationship to be derailed was the fringe diaspora issue,” he said, referring to the murder of Nijjar.

“The reason was the lack of trust. India believed that Canada was actively promoting separatism in India, and Canada believed India was organising violence in Canada. We had a series of meetings between senior Ministers, NSAs of both countries, and agencies at all levels as we set about rebuilding trust. Today, we have reached the highest levels of trust, where the most sensitive areas of cooperation, such as deep tech, defence, and space, are subjects of mutual cooperation,” Mr. Patnaik said.
Cooperation between Canadian and Indian agencies remains at a high level, the High Commissioner added.

articles.title: Xi-Putin-Trump trilateral: Why is it being compared to 1945 Yalta Conference?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The trilateral meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China, on November 19, 2026 is in focus for its implications on the geopolitics of the world.
The three leaders are meeting on the sidelines of the APEC Summit and amidst the looming shadow of the Russia-Ukraine war that has now waged for more than four years.
The Xi-Putin-Jinping meet is being compared with the Yalta Conference of 1945, which led to the establishment of four quarters of post-Nazi Germany and laid the foundations of the United Nations.
The Yalta Conference is the term given to a World War II meeting held in Yalta, Crimea from February 4 to February 11, 1945.

articles.title: Xi hails Russia ties as ‘source of stability’ ahead of trilateral summit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Chinese President opened the two-day APEC gathering with an address to a CEO Summit, where he made a pitch for openness and stable supply chains

Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday hailed relations with Russia “as a source of stability” in a “turbulent” world, even as he welcomed U.S. President Donald Trump with a rare airport reception a day ahead of a trilateral summit in Shenzhen.

On Thursday (November 19, 2026), leaders of the three countries will hold a summit, which Beijing has described as having “groundbreaking significance”. U.S. officials said the three leaders will likely discuss, among other issues, the war in Ukraine, the situation in Iran, global energy stability, and nuclear arms control.

Officials have described the rare trilateral leaders’ summit as more of an exploratory and symbolic meeting, playing down the likelihood of substantive outcomes, either with regard to a possible Russia-Ukraine deal or on the West Asian crisis. Whether they can see eye-to-eye on nuclear disarmament also remains to be seen.
At the same time, Beijing has highlighted the symbolism of the summit happening on its soil, describing it as a landmark moment for what China calls “major country diplomacy”.

In talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), Mr. Xi described China-Russia relations “as a source of stability and certainty in a turbulent world and as a model of a new type of major-power relationship characterised by equality, mutual respect, trust, and win-win cooperation.”

The U.S. President landed in Shenzhen on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), and Mr. Xi welcomed him at the airport with a hug — a rare greeting from the Chinese President, who was reciprocating Mr. Trump similarly receiving him in September at Joint Base Andrews outside Washington.

Chinese President Xi Jinping welcomes US President Donald Trump as he arrives at Shenzhen Airport to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Leaders Summit in Shenzhen, China on November 18, 2026. | Photo Credit: Reuters
The Chinese President opened the two-day APEC gathering with an address to a CEO Summit, where he made a pitch for openness and stable supply chains.

“The world is facing mounting instability, insufficient momentum for economic growth, and a resurgence of unilateralism and protectionism. At the same time, global trade is still growing despite headwinds and emerging technologies are advancing rapidly, reshaping global development,” he said, adding that “the key questions of the age were whether the world would choose openness or closure, cooperation or division, reform or stagnation.”

Mr. Xi called for barriers to trade and investment to be reduced and proposed establishing a World Bay Area Economic Cooperation Alliance. Beijing has been developing the Greater Bay Area, including Shenzhen, Hong Kong and Macau, as an innovation hub.

His remarks came amid continuing China-U.S. trade tensions over a number of issues, including semiconductors and rare earths. Both sides have so far only agreed to extend their trade truce until January, while they continue working on other unresolved issues.

China's President Xi Jinping, right, welcomes President Donald Trump as he arrives at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport in Shenzhen in southern China's Guangdong Province, on November 18, 2026. | Photo Credit: AP

articles.title: West Asia crisis 'largest threat' to energy security ever: IEA
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The report said elsewhere that "increasingly it is falling to consumers — and high prices — to absorb the impact as other buffers are run down"

The crisis in West Asia sparked in February by the U.S. and Israeli bombing of Iran has created the "largest threat" to energy security in history, the International Energy Agency (IEA) warned on Thursday (November 19, 2026).
The agency said in its flagship annual World Energy Outlook that consumers were increasingly footing the bill as the world runs out of ways to absorb the impact of the conflict on energy supplies.
The crisis, just like previous energy shocks, would certainly leave "lasting marks", the agency warned.
ALSO WATCH Watch: At least 40 energy facilities ‘severely’ affected: IEA Chief

Gulf countries have been struggling to export oil since Iran began blockading the Strait of Hormuz and targeting tankers in the area, following U.S. and Israeli strikes that sparked the crisis in February.
Despite attempts by the United States to escort vessels through the channel — which pre-crisis carried about one-fifth of global oil shipments — supply lines remain severely disrupted.

"The Strait of Hormuz crisis has created the largest threat to energy security in history, one that dwarfs the scale of the oil shocks of the 1970s," IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol wrote in his foreword to the report.

He highlighted the efforts countries had taken to protect households, with producing nations bringing more supplies into the market and using alternative routes, and China buying less from international markets.
"Governments have intervened to try and provide some shelter for consumers, but they have nonetheless faced higher prices and, in some cases, shortfalls of supply," Mr. Birol wrote.
The report said elsewhere that "increasingly it is falling to consumers — and high prices — to absorb the impact as other buffers are run down".
Mr. Birol had struck a more hopeful tone in July when he wrote that the oil market was still benefiting from "several cushioning factors".

The IEA's report comes as nations meet for the COP31 climate talks in Turkiye, with governments under pressure to tackle climate change after a year of searing heatwaves and wildfires in Europe, and deadly floods in Nepal.

articles.title: IIIT-H students develop web plugin to translate text into Indian Sign Language
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The tool is a simple plugin that lets you select text on a web page, producing a 3D avatar that signs in the Indian Sign Language

The Indian Sign Language (ISL) uses gestures to represent complex words and sentences and has its own grammar and word order. People with hearing impairments find it a challenge to read content online. To address this gap, Masthan Sharif Shaik and Mohammed Raza, third-year BTech. students from the Center for Visual Information Technology (CVIT), IIIT-Hyderabad, under the supervision of Prof. C.V. Jawahar and Prof. Vinay Namboodiri (University of Bath, U.K.), developed a cost-effective plugin that can be added to any website.

The plugin can run inside a browser in real time, without any real hardware or an AI model running on a server. “Websites today support captions, screen readers, and high-contrast modes, but almost none of them can show content in sign language. Existing signing avatars are either costly motion-capture systems, heavy AI models that need powerful GPUs, or systems built from sign notation – all of which require linguistic experts and also tend to move robotically,” Sharif said.

The researchers first took the official Indian Sign Language Research And Training Centre’s sign-language dictionary videos and used computer vision to recover each signer’s 3D body, hand and finger movements. “Automatic reconstruction, however, often gets fingers wrong, and in sign language a wrong finger can change the meaning. So, we built an annotation tool, Gizmo, to correct only the few key poses of each sign instead of every frame,” Sharif said.

There is an offline preprocessing that takes place where sentences are converted into ISL word order. For example, a sentence such as “He will come home” in ISL becomes “He home come”. When a sentence like the former is highlighted and the ‘Click To Sign’ button is selected, the stored motion for each sign is fetched, and the signs are blended smoothly, allowing the avatar to sign the whole sentence fluidly. Words without a sign are fingerspelled letter by letter.

The movements are more natural in this case because the avatar replays motion captured from real signers rather than motion generated from notation. Additionally, what makes this task unique is that it all happens without a GPU. “The heavy computer-vision work happens once, offline, when the sign dictionary is built. Viewing a sentence only replays and blends stored motion together, which an ordinary laptop handles”, says Sharif.

When tested on deaf and hard-of-hearing signers, the ISL signers understood about 89% of sentences signed by the avatar. However, the lack of facial features in the avatar was cited as a drawback because expressions typically include grammar in ISL, as well as signs that change form in context. “We will work to incorporate this in our next iteration,” says Sharif.

“Indian Sign language (ISL) seriously lacks resources and technologies”, explains Prof. Jawahar. The group is working in two directions – Sign Language Synthesis as well as Sign Language Understanding. The plugin is related to sign language synthesis from text on low cost commodity hardware.

Existing signing avatars are either costly motion-capture systems, heavy AI models that need powerful GPUs, or systems built from sign notation – all of which require linguistic experts and also tend to move robotically,” Sharif said.

articles.title: GTA VI is here, and India has taken the day off
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Grand Theft Auto VI is a homecoming, and this time a good part of the city was built in Bengaluru

This week, Grand Theft Auto VI landed on Blinkit, in a collectible box available in select areas across 11 cities. There is no disc inside, only a download code, because Rockstar is selling the game purely as a download, even in stores. That makes for instant gratification of a new kind: the most anticipated game in years can now reach your doorstep in minutes, about as quickly as a loaf of bread, with the code ready to redeem the moment it arrives. Blinkit co-founder Albinder Dhindsa announced the offering on X on November 18, noting that it had taken 13 years for the game to arrive. It is a very 2026 way to launch a game, and an apt one, given that Grand Theft Auto has always found its way to Indian players through whichever door happened to be open.

The game itself costs ₹5,999 for the Standard Edition and ₹7,499 for the Ultimate Edition on both PlayStation and Xbox, which is almost exactly double what Grand Theft Auto V cost here at launch. In dollars, though, Indian buyers pay about US$63 for the Standard Edition versus the $79.99 charged in the United States, and pre-order customers also receive the Vintage Vice City Pack. It is on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S only for now, with no PC version announced, which is a shift for a series so many Indians first met on a computer, though Grand Theft Auto V took the same route and reached PC in 2015.

GTA 6 is now live on Blinkit! 🎮 It took 13 years for GTA 6 to be released. In the meantime, we built Blinkit so that you can get the game delivered in minutes. We've launched it in select areas of Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad, Noida, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune, Kolkata & Ahmedabad (launching in more cities between today and tomorrow). We'll deliver a physical box with a download code inside (the box is a nice collectible for your shelf). Get yours now and start downloading so you're ready to play from 19th November. Expecting a suspicious number of sick leaves over the next few days 😮‍💨

In solidarity, consumer electronics brand boAt offered employees an optional day off on November 19, announcing it with the caption Out of office. Into Vice City. In Chennai, interior design firm Inde by ChairsCarte declared a holiday for its staff, interns and freelancers, calling it “just a day off for a game we’ve waited years for”.

For a generation of Indian players, the first port of call was the neighbourhood cyber café. Vice City and San Andreas, which defined the series in the early 2000s, were among the first open worlds many Indians explored, playing on rented computers by the hour, often between rounds of Counter-Strike, long before gaming became a career in India. San Andreas also gave us cheat codes, strings of nonsense such as HESOYAM, which replenished health, armour and cash in one go. For those who grew up typing them, they remain shorthand for nostalgia.

Even Indians who have never owned a copy know the series, thanks to its meme culture. The grey-and-red Wasted screen from GTA V, which appears when a character dies, has spent years slapped onto videos of people and animals spectacularly failing at something. Big Smoke’s exasperated yell at CJ for losing a train in San Andreas became so widely shared that Rockstar later named a GTA V trophy Better Than CJ in its honour. But the longest-running joke was about the wait. As the sequel failed to materialise, “We got X before GTA 6” became the Internet’s way of reacting to anything improbable. India took to it enthusiastically, with electronics retailer Croma fuelling another round when the game was delayed to November 19, 2026.
Your KRA is updated to completing missions and side quests 🎮 https://t.co/x1xSmUIPqU

Grand Theft Auto V arrived in India in September 2013, priced at around ₹3,000 for the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360. But its second life here began after PUBG Mobile was banned in September 2020. Several of India’s biggest streamers, including Dynamo and MortaL, turned to other games, GTA V among them, and roleplay helped make it a mainstay of Indian livestreaming.

A roleplay server is a fan-run version of GTA V’s online world where players invent characters with names, jobs and backstories, from cab drivers and paramedics to cops and small-time crooks, and inhabit them for hours. Soulcity, launched by S8UL and Velocity Gaming in early 2023, became one of India’s biggest GTA V roleplay servers and helped create a new breed of gaming star. S8UL co-founder Lokesh Jain, better known as 8Bit Goldy, played a character called Rocket Singh on the server. The scene grew big enough for S8UL to sign creators such as Sunny Jha, aka Pitaji Playz, specifically for its GTA roleplay roster.
Gamers watch a screen showing the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) at a gaming centre in Buenos Aires on the day of the highly anticipated video game's release. | Photo Credit: AFP

One of the biggest differences between GTA VI and its predecessors for Indian players is how much of it was made here. Rockstar India’s Bengaluru studio reportedly has the largest team of any Rockstar office working on the game, with around 1,615 developers, and media reports credit it with building Vice Beach, a location on the map. Its roots go back to Dhruva Interactive, founded by Rajesh Rao in Bengaluru in 1997 and considered India’s oldest game developer when Rockstar folded it into Rockstar India in 2019. Rockstar India was established in 2016 and contributed to Red Dead Redemption 2 before turning to Leonida.

The game follows Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, two small-time criminals drawn into a conspiracy across Leonida, Rockstar’s fictional Florida, after a job goes wrong. Lucia is the series’ first female lead since it moved into three dimensions. The Vice City she drives through is a contemporary one, a far cry from the pastel-hued 1980s city many Indian players grew up with.

articles.title: This 2D rhythm platformer video game is an ode to India’s multiplicities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Suri: The Seventh Note by Tathvamasi Studios is set in a universe controlled by evil music. The game was launched in October

The story of Suri: The Seventh Note, a 2D video game by Bengaluru-based Tathvamasi Studios, is set in a world corrupted by an evil version of music. Everything in this universe moves in tune with that nefarious sonic presence. The protagonist, Ajira, must find a fruit located at the centre of the island to save her mother from certain death. Soon, she realises her actions shall determine the fate of the island itself.

Suri: The Seventh Note is the brainchild of Glen Martin from Kochi, founder of Tathvamasi Studios, who is also the game director of the video. He is joined by Chitrak Srivastava, co-founder and the game’s art director. The game was launched on Playstation Store and Steam in October.

Glen, formerly a data scientist, found himself immersed in game-making during the pandemic. He began by making smaller games, with friends from different places joining him on a Discord server to help. “When we started to build the game, it was not meant to be a project. But once we realised its potential, we began to think about what could be unique about this game,” says Glen.
Glen Martin and Chitrak Srivastava | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT

“At that point, I was playing a parry-focused combat game called Sekiro. It’s a very hard game, and I am not good at it. But then I saw a lot of streamers play the game skilfully, without even taking a single hit, and I realised that when the game is played at that level, it has a certain rhythmic quality to it,” he adds. “The sounds of the sword clinking, the jumps and movements, everything felt choreographed.”
This ultimately led him to turn Suri… into a rhythm platformer game.

Suri... is a mix of two different games: rhythm and platformer. Rhythm games are music-themed action games that assess a player’s sense of timing and metre, while platformers are a sub-genre where a main character moves through uneven terrain and suspended platforms.

“There are very few games that have done this before, so our well of references was limited. In Suri..., the world moves to the rhythm. All the things that you would normally interact with in a regular platformer, like traps, obstacles, etc., are all tied to the rhythm in our game. You have to listen to the music to understand when a thing would move up and down or when a leaf would open or close and so on,” explains Glen. “When played well, it feels like dancing through levels.”

In 2024, Suri was one of five games at the inaugural edition of PlayStation’s India Hero Project, an incubator programme from Sony Interactive Entertainment. This ultimately allowed Glen to quit his job and hire more people.
A still from Suri: The Seventh Note | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT

One of the most intriguing aspects about Suri is the world it is set in. “Suri is set in our own version of mythical India. While we are inspired by Indian ethos and culture, we have not tried to mimic it or take things from it directly. We’ve tried to create our own world,” says Glen.

Chitrak says, “We wanted to create something that belongs to those places we grew up in. Usually when you play these games, they mostly have European or Japanese settings. We wanted to find something that we could relate to and have the world explore that side of our culture. That was the north star for us, while we began developing this world.”

articles.title: Samsung Electronics downplays concerns about neocloud firms and AI bubble
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Shares of neocloud firms including CoreWeave, which rents out computing capacity to tech firms, have been hit by concerns that their ​debt-fuelled data center expansions ‌could backfire if AI demand slows

Samsung Electronics , the world’s ​top maker of memory chips, on Wednesday downplayed concerns that highly ‌leveraged neocloud providers could fuel a broader AI ​bubble, saying they account for only a small ⁠share of the overall market.

“Neoclouds represent a relatively smaller and limited portion of the overall market, approximately 8%,” said Kim Yong-kwan, president ‌and head of corporate management, strategy and operation at Samsung’s component business division, at a Morgan ‌Stanley conference in Singapore.
“We do not expect these ‌concerns ⁠to pose a significant threat to the broader ⁠AI growth trajectory.”

Shares of neocloud firms including CoreWeave, which rents out computing capacity to tech firms, have been hit by concerns that their ​debt-fuelled data center expansions ‌could backfire if AI demand slows.

The departure of Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia this month could also tighten funding for smaller, highly leveraged neocloud companies that have ‌helped fuel the industry’s rapid expansion, analysts and ​investors have said.

Kang Suk-chae, Samsung’s Head of Foundry Sales & Marketing, said the current AI investment ⁠boom was structural rather than cyclical, with long-term contracts between chipmakers and customers providing greater visibility over demand and supply.
He ‌said the current boom differed from previous cycles in which speculative investment ultimately led to overcapacity.
“In short, today’s investment is not a result of speculation, but actual tangible demand,” Kang said, saying the ongoing chip shortage would “persist for the foreseeable future.”

He said Samsung’s foundry business, which ‌competes with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, has diversified manufacturing footprints “to mitigate supply chains” and ​offers “a one-stop solution” that includes memory and advanced packaging.
Kim reiterated Samsung’s previous statement that it ⁠would carry out its remaining shareholder returns through a mix of cash ⁠dividends and a “substantial” share repurchase and cancellation program.
He said the company had a number of factors ‌to consider, including capital expenditures, before announcing details on its shareholder return package in January.

articles.title: Cyclone 'Akvan' LIVE updates: Over one lakh evacuated in Odisha as landfall likely near Gopalpur; red alert for three A.P. districts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The IMD says the corridor for landfall, likely on Nov. 20 noon, stretches from Andhra's Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh to Odisha's Puri
Severe cyclonic storm ‘Akvan’ continues to move northwards with a speed of 17 kmph, the IMD said in its latest update on Thursday afternoon (November 19, 2026).

It is likely to move north-northwestward and cross North Andhra Pradesh & Yanam and South Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri, close to Gopalpur, by noon of 20th November, 2026 with the maximum sustained wind speed of 90-100 kmph gusting to 110 kmph, it added.

The Srikakulam and Vizianagaram district administrations are on high alert ahead of Cyclone Akvan, which is expected to cross the coast near Gopalpur in Odisha on Friday (November 20, 2026). Srikakulam, which suffered heavily in the two recent cyclones, Arnab and Murasu , is ready to face the new challenge.

Srikakulam Collector Swapnil Dinakar Pundkar and other officials visited Donkuru and other villages of Ichchapuram , on the Andhra Pradesh-Odisha border, to review the preparedness of local officials. Ichchapuram, Sompeta and other areas were badly affected by floods in the Bahuda after the earlier cyclones.

Vizianagaram Collector S. Ramsundar Reddy reviewed the situation at the coastal villages of Pusapatirega and Bhogapuram and asked officials to take necessary measures ahead of the cyclone. He said fishermen had been advised not to venture into the sea for the next few days on the government’s orders.
The IMD on Thursday (November 19, 2026) forecast heavy rain in the southern districts of West Bengal in the next two days as cyclonic storm ‘Akvan’ approaches the east coast.
Kolkata and other southern districts of the state experienced overnight rain as a result of the weather system, it said.
The coastal districts of South 24 Parganas and Purba Medinipur, along with Kolkata, Howrah and Paschim Medinipur, received overnight rain due to the weather conditions, it said.
Heavy rain is likely over North 24 Parganas, Paschim Medinipur, Jhargram and Bankura, the IMD said.

Thunderstorms, accompanied by gusty winds reaching speeds of 30-40 kmph, will occur over Kolkata and other south Bengal districts till Saturday, it said. The Met office advised fishermen not to venture into the sea till Saturday (November 21, 2026), as conditions will be rough owing to the severe cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal.

Odisha on Thursday (November 19, 2026) stepped up evacuation of people, positioning of disaster response forces and emptying of reservoirs in southern and coastal districts as the Severe Cyclonic Storm ‘Akvan’ is expected cross the State’s coast, close to east of Gopalpur, by noon of November 20.

Office of Special Relief Commissioner said more than one lakh people, including close to 10,000 pregnant women, have been shifted to safer places. While Ganjam district under which Gopalpur lies alone has shifted over 50,000 people, Gajapati and Kandhamal districts have relocated 16,000 and 3000 people respectively.

articles.title: TVK MLA V.S. Babu, who defeated M.K. Stalin in Kolathur, passes away
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: He had been admitted to MGM Healthcare, Chennai, with a prolonged respiratory illness

Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) MLA V.S. Babu, who defeated DMK president and former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin in the Kolathur Assembly constituency in the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly election, died following a cardiac arrest on Thursday (November 19, 2026). He was 75.

Mr. Babu was admitted to MGM Hospital in Aminjikarai, Chennai, on September 9 with a respiratory illness. According to the medical bulletin issued by the hospital, he was under intensive care. His condition continued to deteriorate, and he subsequently suffered a cardiac arrest and died on November 19 at 2.24 p.m.
Mr. Babu started his political career in the DMK as an area secretary and went on to become the party’s north Chennai district secretary.

He was first elected to the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly from the Purasawalkam Assembly constituency in the 2006 Assembly election as a DMK candidate. Following the 2008 delimitation exercise, the Purasawalkam constituency ceased to exist, and many areas falling under it became part of the newly formed Kolathur Assembly constituency.

Mr. Babu, then a local face of the DMK, reportedly played a considerable role in Mr. Stalin’s victory in the Kolathur Assembly constituency in the 2011 election. After 2011, Mr. Babu stayed away from politics for a while before joining the AIADMK in 2016. Earlier this year, he joined the TVK in the presence of party president and now Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay.
With his passing, the number of vacancies in the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly has risen to six.

articles.title: Supreme Court to commence final hearing of pleas on marital rape in December
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Under the exception clause of Section 375 of the Indian Penal Code, now repealed and replaced by the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his wife, the wife not being minor, is not rape
The Supreme Court on Thursday (November 19, 2026) said it would list a batch of petitions pertaining to the contentious issue of marital rape for final hearing in December.

The Supreme Court is seized of petitions raising the vexed legal question of whether a husband should enjoy immunity from prosecution for the offence of rape if he forces his wife, who is not a minor, to have sex.

Under the exception clause of Section 375 of the Indian Penal Code, now repealed and replaced by the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his wife, the wife not being minor, is not rape.
Even under the new law, exception 2 to Section 63 (rape) says that “sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his own wife, the wife not being under eighteen years of age, is not rape”.
The petitions were listed for hearing during the day before a Bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana.

Senior advocate Indira Jaising, who is appearing in the matter, told the Supreme Court that the Bench is scheduled to hear a part-heard matter at 2 p.m. during the day. She urged the Bench that the marital rape matter be listed for hearing in December, as today it may not come up since the Bench is seized of a part-heard matter.
“We will either have it on December 2-3 or on December 9-10. Today, it is not possible. We are trying to finish the part-heard matter today,” the CJI said.
One of the lawyers appearing in the marital rape case requested the Bench to list the matter on December 9 and 10.
“We will fix it on December 9 or December 10,” the Bench said, adding, “We will try to hear it before the winter break”.
The winter break in the Supreme Court would commence from December 21.
On September 9, the Centre had told the Bench that the counter affidavit filed earlier by it in the lead case may be treated as its reply in other petitions as well.

The Bench had then observed that it would examine aspects such as whether prosecution can be sustained if the marital rape exception survives, and whether the exception itself was constitutionally valid.

🏛️ National & Polity 📅 19 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Supreme Court to commence final hearing of pleas on marital rape in December

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

Under the exception clause of Section 375 of the Indian Penal Code, now repealed and replaced by the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his wife, the wife not being minor, is not rape

The Supreme Court on Thursday (November 19, 2026) said it would list a batch of petitions pertaining to the contentious issue of marital rape for final hearing in December.

The Supreme Court is seized of petitions raising the vexed legal question of whether a husband should enjoy immunity from prosecution for the offence of rape if he forces his wife, who is not a minor, to have sex.

Under the exception clause of Section 375 of the Indian Penal Code, now repealed and replaced by the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his wife, the wife not being minor, is not rape.

Even under the new law, exception 2 to Section 63 (rape) says that “sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his own wife, the wife not being under eighteen years of age, is not rape”.

The petitions were listed for hearing during the day before a Bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana.

Senior advocate Indira Jaising, who is appearing in the matter, told the Supreme Court that the Bench is scheduled to hear a part-heard matter at 2 p.m. during the day. She urged the Bench that the marital rape matter be listed for hearing in December, as today it may not come up since the Bench is seized of a part-heard matter.

“We will either have it on December 2-3 or on December 9-10. Today, it is not possible. We are trying to finish the part-heard matter today,” the CJI said.

One of the lawyers appearing in the marital rape case requested the Bench to list the matter on December 9 and 10.

“We will fix it on December 9 or December 10,” the Bench said, adding, “We will try to hear it before the winter break”.

The winter break in the Supreme Court would commence from December 21.

On September 9, the Centre had told the Bench that the counter affidavit filed earlier by it in the lead case may be treated as its reply in other petitions as well.

The Bench had then observed that it would examine aspects such as whether prosecution can be sustained if the marital rape exception survives, and whether the exception itself was constitutionally valid.

articles.title: Author Samina Mishra explores borders, identity and citizenship through children’s eyes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The filmmaker and author examines how art and storytelling can open up conversations about society, equality and constitutional values

What do borders mean to a child? Is it a line separating two countries, a language that makes someone feel like an outsider, or the invisible divisions that determine who belongs and who does not? For filmmaker and children’s author Samina Mishra, these questions have informed much of her work with children, particularly those growing up in circumstances where displacement, identity and belonging shape everyday life. Samina, who will be in Visakhapatnam for the Vizag Junior Literary Fest this month, believes that young people must have the space to question the divisions that shape their world.

Her engagement with these ideas took shape through a three-year association with Simurgh Centre in Delhi, where she conducted art workshops with children from Khirkee, a south Delhi neighbourhood home to several Afghan refugee families. The monthly Simurgh Children’s Art Workshop, designed for children aged nine to 15, offered them an opportunity to watch films, discuss their themes and respond through art. For children with limited access to spaces for play, leisure and creative expression, these sessions opened up possibilities for engaging with the world beyond their immediate circumstances.

During the first year, Samina selected short films from different countries, particularly those that communicated visually with little or no dialogue, allowing children from different linguistic backgrounds to participate. One of the films screened was The Present , a Palestinian short about a father and son attempting to buy a gift and the difficulties they encounter at checkpoints.
“It initiated conversations about lines and borders. That is also what my book Lines explores,” she says.

In her workshops for children, the idea of a line extends beyond geographical boundaries. Through discussions and art-based exercises, children examine the many ways people are separated, whether by language, caste, community or circumstances.

The conversations also draw from their experiences of moving to unfamiliar places and negotiating questions of identity and belonging. By encouraging children to approach these subjects through their own experiences, Samina hopes to make larger social questions more accessible.

Her interest in children’s understanding of society formed another project called ‘Hum Hindustani’, a research initiative she conceived and executed, which examines citizenship through the constitutional principles of liberty, equality and fraternity. Part of the Transforming Education for Sustainable Futures (TESF) India network, the project engages children in Grades 6 to 9 across three locations: Shaheen Bagh in Delhi, rural Firozpur in Punjab and Kitab Mahal, a library serving Dalit and Muslim children in Govandi, Mumbai.

Each location represents a distinct social and political experience, from the citizens’ protest at Shaheen Bagh to the farmers’ movement in Punjab and community-led learning initiatives in Govandi. Through arts-based exercises and documentary interviews with children and adults, the project explores how constitutional promises relate to the realities of growing up in different social settings.

“The initiative documents children’s creative responses through artwork and poetry,” says Samina. Its Hum Hindustani Poetry Podcast brings their writing into conversation with writers, artists and educators. Available in English and Hindi, the recordings offer an insight into how young people interpret citizenship through their everyday experiences.

For Samina, the project also addresses the marginalisation of children’s voices in conversations about democracy and society. “While children are frequently discussed in the context of education, welfare and public policy, their own interpretations receive far less attention,” she says and adds, “Children must be recognised as individuals capable of thinking about their rights, relationships and responsibilities.”

Currently, ‘Hum Hindustani’ is also engaging with children at Yellow Streets, a community learning space for those from vulnerable and underserved neighbourhoods, through workshops involving two animal films . Samina is also working on a picture book with Tulika Publishers.

At the Vizag Junior Literary Festival, scheduled for November 21 and 22 at Hawa Mahal in Visakhapatnam, Samina will conduct two sessions for children aged eight to 12 and 13 to 16. Each 90-minute session will draw on the workshops developed around the themes explored in Lines. Through creative exercises and conversations, participants will be encouraged to examine separation, identity and belonging from their own perspectives, without being led towards predetermined answers. At the literary festival, she hopes to encourage young participants to look beyond familiar definitions and consider a question that has occupied much of her work: what does it take to make room for everyone?
