articles.title: Grab every chance given by ECI for reinclusion before November 30 deadline, Supreme Court tells deleted voters
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Court asks ECI to provide details of the number of applications it received for inclusion, deletion and correction of names; Bench to take stock of situation on December 2

The Supreme Court on Thursday (November 19, 2026) urged deleted voters to rigorously test the Election Commission of India (ECI)’s assurances that no elector, mistakenly branded ‘absent, shifted, deceased, duplicate’ or ASDD, will be left out of the electoral roll during the special enumeration phase of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).
The court said voters can hold the ECI to account only by first acting on every opportunity thrown at them by the poll body before the special enumeration phase concludes on November 30.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said it would take stock on December 2, when a complete picture would emerge about the ground reality, particularly the extent of access deleted voters really had to enumeration forms. The court asked the EC to provide in a tabular form the number of applications received for inclusions, deletions and correction of names in the electoral rolls during the special enumeration phase.

The court also indicated that it may even extend the November 30 deadline, if necessary. “But for now you [voters] see what happens when you utilise this window [till November 30]. See what is the extent of their [EC] accommodation,” Justice Joymalya Bagchi observed.
The brief exchange came during the hearing of a petition filed by activists Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri, represented by advocates Prashant Bhushan, Cheryl D’Souza, and Neha Rathi.

These petitioners had highlighted that the ECI was compelling ASDD voters in Delhi to apply for reinclusion by filing Form 6 and by misrepresenting themselves as fresh applicants. They said such misrepresentation was a criminal offence attracting imprisonment.

In a previous hearing on October 28, the top court made it clear that the EC was in “error” to force pre-existing voters, deleted from the electoral rolls, to apply as new voters under Form 6 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.

The court had, instead, suggested the EC to allow ASDD voters to either apply through enumeration forms or Form 8 (used by registered voters to update personal details like change of residence, etc) during the special enumeration phase.

On November 14, the EC informed the court through a supplementary affidavit that ASDD voters would be allowed to submit duly-filled enumeration forms communicating their current ordinary residence. Those who had not shifted their residence had to only provide a statement giving reasons for not filling up the enumeration form earlier. Electors who shifted residence within the same State were not required to file Form 8.

Further, the EC had made it clear that those who had already applied through Form 6 would not face criminal prosecution. The poll body said these directions had been communicated to electoral authorities across multiple States in a communication dated November 6.

On Thursday, Mr. Bhushan alleged that there had hardly been any ground-level implementation of the court’s October 28 suggestions. He said the enumeration forms were downloadable only from November 19.
The senior lawyer submitted that though the directions were sent on November 6, the standard operating procedure and timeline for implementing them was issued only on November 17.

articles.title: Graca Machel conferred Indira Gandhi Prize; Sonia Gandhi recalls shared ideals of social justice
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In her acceptance speech, the humanitarian said India and Africa shared a legacy that needed to be carried forward

Mozambican politician and women’s rights advocate Graca Machel was conferred the 2025 Indira Gandhi Prize for Peace, Disarmament and Development on Thursday, coinciding with the former Prime Minister’s 109th birth anniversary.
Sonia Gandhi, who heads the Indira Gandhi Memorial Trust, presented the award, which comprised a citation and a cash prize of ₹1 crore.
Ms. Gandhi said Ms. Machel’s life and work reflected Indira Gandhi’s ideals, particularly the commitment to social justice, human dignity and equality.
Both Indira Gandhi and Ms. Machel believed in people’s power to shape their own futures, she said.
Their lives, Ms. Gandhi noted, demonstrated that leadership was measured by the courage to challenge injustice and the commitment to bring about change.

Tracing Ms. Machel’s journey from Mozambique’s liberation struggle to her work on women’s and children’s rights, Ms. Gandhi recalled that Ms. Machel became the country’s first Minister of Education and Culture after it gained independence in 1975. During her tenure, school participation rose from 40% to over 90% among boys and 75% among girls.

Ms. Machel was also the wife of Mozambique’s first President, Samora Machel, serving as First Lady until his death in 1986. In 1998, she married former South African President Nelson Mandela, becoming the only woman to have been First Lady of two countries.
“Education, for her, meant giving a new generation the opportunity to shape its future,” Ms. Gandhi said, drawing a parallel with Indira Gandhi’s emphasis on education and nation-building.
Recalling the former Prime Minister’s words, she said, “Peace, like freedom and progress, is indivisible.”

Ms. Gandhi also referred to Ms. Machel’s landmark 1996 United Nations report on the impact of armed conflict on children, which helped shape the international response to the suffering of children in conflict zones.
“Her work reminds us that peace is not simply the absence of conflict. It must also enable communities to rebuild their lives and look towards the future,” she said.
Ms. Gandhi said there could be no lasting peace without justice and no meaningful development where violence and insecurity prevailed.

articles.title: OPEC share in India’s crude imports drops to 27.4% in Apr-Oct amid West Asia flare-ups
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: During the mentioned period, India’s crude oil imports spurred about 2.7% to 146.6 million metric tonnes (MMT)

The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries’ (OPEC) share in India’s crude oil basket declined sharply to 27.4% during April-October of the current fiscal, against 38.5% in the corresponding period last year, according to the latest provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC).

The decline potentially reflects a shift in India’s crude procurement strategy as the country navigates shipping disruptions and geopolitical uncertainties arising from the continuing conflict in West Asia.
During the seven-month period, India’s crude oil imports increased 2.7% to 146.6 million metric tonnes (MMT).
Without identifying individual countries, PPAC data showed that supplies from the Eurasian region accounted for 43.8% of India’s crude oil import basket, while the Middle East contributed 36%.
South America accounted for 10.6% of imports, followed by Africa at 6.6% and North America at 3%.
The changing sourcing pattern indicates a growing diversification of India’s crude oil procurement, with supplies from outside the traditional Middle Eastern market gaining a larger share.

On the petroleum products trade front, diesel accounted for the largest share of India’s exports at 43.4% during the reported period. Petrol and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) followed with shares of 22.4% and 10%, respectively.
On the import side, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) constituted the largest component, accounting for 50.5% of total petroleum product imports, followed by petroleum coke (petcoke) at 18.3%.
Petroleum product exports remain an important component of India’s external energy trade to contain the impact on its net oil and gas import bill.
Further, PPAC data released on Wednesday showed that petroleum product export volumes declined 13.5% year-on-year during April-October, even as their export value increased approximately 47%.

articles.title: Japanese PM Takaichi says Russia, Japan will keep talking as ties remain chilled
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The last bilateral in-person talks between Japanese and Russian leaders were held between then-Prime Minister Shinzo Abe and Putin in September 2019, during the Eastern Economic Forum in the Russian city of Vladivostok.

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said on Thursday (November 19, 2026) that she and Russian President Vladimir Putin held talks and agreed to keep communicating in the first such encounter between the two countries' leaders in seven years.

Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, she said she raised the issue of Moscow's treatment of Japanese businesses in Russia and urged Putin to release a Japanese journalist detained for alleged spying during their meeting late Wednesday (November 18, 2026) in Shenzhen, China.
“We reached an agreement to maintain communication at various levels, including direct contact between the president and myself,” Ms. Takaichi said.
Japan's ties with Russia have long been strained by a territorial dispute dating back decades.

Japan lodged a protest with Russia in October over the arrest of a Japanese journalist working for the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper on suspicion of spying, demanding that Moscow provide an explanation, consular access and humane treatment.

Moscow recently seized control of some local subsidiaries of Japan Tobacco, the largest cigarette maker in Russia, and the company reported it expects a 724 billion yen ($4.5 billion) loss for this year due to the takeover.

Earlier, Japan Tobacco had forecast a 662 billion yen profit for the financial year ending December 31. The company said it has not given up legal ownership of the Russia-based subsidiaries or withdrawn from operating in Russia.

Tensions rose in August after Mr. Putin visited Iturup, one of four Russian-controlled islands off Japan's northern coast that Tokyo also claims. Earlier this month, Tokyo protested after two Russian aircraft briefly violated Japanese airspace off southwestern Japan.

The last bilateral in-person talks between Japanese and Russian leaders were held between then-Prime Minister Shinzo Abe and Mr. Putin in September 2019, during the Eastern Economic Forum in the Russian city of Vladivostok.

Mr. Putin is attending the annual APEC summit for the first time in nine years. He, Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump held a summit meeting on Thursday (November 19, 2026) after the APEC gathering, an event that seems to underscore Japan's diminished role as a global power.
Ms. Takaichi herself was given a very minimal reception on her arrival in Shenzhen, provoking speculation over a deliberate snub by her hosts.
When asked, Ms. Takaichi said she did not believe the summit between Mr. Xi, Mr. Trump and Mr. Putin would undermine Japan's interests.

articles.title: Riyadh's tallest building damaged as Saudi reports new Houthi attacks
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Iran-backed Houthis have stepped up their attacks against Saudi Arabia in recent weeks, striking targets including airports, energy infrastructure, military sites and Riyadh's financial district

A skyscraper in Riyadh housing the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund was damaged on Thursday (November 19, 2026), witnesses told AFP , as the kingdom reported new attacks by Yemen's Houthis.
Saudi Arabia has been battling a surge in attacks since fighting reignited in neighbouring Yemen's civil war, where Riyadh backs the internationally recognised government against the Houthis.
In the early hours of Thursday (November 19, 2026), AFP journalists in the Saudi capital reported a powerful blast was heard.
Around the same time, civil defence authorities issued a warning for "potential danger" but said minutes later that the danger had passed.
The Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis said it had "addressed a missile threat launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Riyadh".
"Initial assessment indicates the impact of debris, with material damage currently being surveyed," said coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki.
Witnesses later told AFP that Riyadh's Public Investment Fund Tower, which at 80 storeys is the tallest in the city, had been damaged.
"The facade is damaged across several floors, with windows blown out," said one person who requested anonymity.
"The damage also affected some of the buildings surrounding PIF tower, causing the glass facades on some to shatter. Some of the buildings are residential," the witness added.
Two other witnesses confirmed the damage to the tower, which AFP was unable to visit.
Since early September, most employees in the building had been working remotely, they told AFP .
Standing 385 metres high, the PIF tower dominates Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District, which acts as a showcase for Saudi Arabia's economic ambitions.

articles.title: Rohingya a ‘distinct lineage’ close to Bangladeshis and Burmese: Study
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The International Court of Justice held that Myanmar had committed genocide against the Muslim minority Rohingya in the north Rakhine State

The Rohingya are a distinct genetic group with genomic ancestry closer to Bangladeshis but considerable genetic mixture from the Burmese lineage. While this isn’t surprising from a linguistic-cultural perspective, it is the first such comprehensive study from a genomic analysis perspective.

“Burmese” here is a stand-in for East and Southeast Asian ancestry in general. The study underlines what is now a basic principle of human population genetics that all ethnic populations are a result of intermingling of multiple population groups through history.

The analysis comes on the heels of a Thursday (November 19) verdict by the International Court of Justice. In a 9-6 ruling, the court held that Myanmar had committed genocide against the Muslim minority Rohingya in the north Rakhine State. This was the verdict on a 2019 case brought to the court by The Gambia in which it accused the Myanmar government of trying to destroy the Rohingya.
The Burmese state has tried to portray the Rohingya as “outsiders” from Bangladesh to justify atrocities against them.

The genetics study, which appeared on November 17 in the peer-reviewed journal Scientific Reports , does not say anything about citizenship, but notes: “This study addresses a critical void in the evolutionary history of a deeply marginalised group and unequivocally reinforces that modern human populations are intricate mosaics of diverse ancestral lineages, fundamentally shaped by historical migrations and gene flow that transcend contemporary political boundaries.”

The main authors of the study are affiliated with a range of institutions including the Banaras Hindu University (BHU), Varanasi; BRIC-Centre for DNA Fingerprinting and Diagnostics (CDFD), Hyderabad; the University of Dhaka, Bangladesh; University of Calcutta; and Amity University, Uttar Pradesh.

“Our analyses reveal a complex genomic architecture that closely mirrors their linguistic affiliations. The Rohingya exhibit a foundational genetic affinity with eastern South Asian Indo-European speaking populations, predominantly aligning with present-day Bangladeshi communities,” the authors report.

The Rohingya migrated into the Arakan region within the last millennium and, following this, the ancestral Rohingya mixed with those with Southeast Asian ancestry from local Myanmar-related populations, they underline.

For their analysis, the researchers took blood samples from 25 Rohingya volunteers at the Cox’s Bazar refugee camp in Bangladesh, with informed consent and ethics approval from the University of Dhaka. For comparison they sampled 45 neighbours: 27 Bangladeshi Muslims, nine Bangladeshi Hindus, and nine people from the Bawm tribal community. They then merged these results with published data from around the world, for a final dataset of 2,217 people. Each person’s DNA was read at about 370,000 key places along the genome, where nucleotide letters commonly differ between people.

articles.title: Israel army says it completed ground operation in central Gaza
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Hamas denounced a "blatant ceasefire violation," while the military said the rare ground incursion was a response to Hamas ceasefire violations in the area
Israel's military said that a ground operation involving tanks in central Gaza that began the previous day despite a U.S.-brokered ceasefire had come to an end on Thursday (November 19, 2026).

The Defence Ministry's body in charge of civilian affairs in Palestinian territories, Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories (COGAT), said in a statement that Palestinians would again be free to move in the targeted areas near the Al-Bureij and Nuseirat refugee camps.

"We would like to inform you that the activity has ended, and the Salah al-Din axis has been reopened," COGAT said in an Arabic-language statement on Facebook, referring to the war-shattered territory's main thoroughfare.

On Wednesday (November 18, 2026), the Israeli military said it had launched an operation in a Hamas-controlled area of central Gaza, beyond the so-called "Yellow Line" which separates areas under Israeli military and Hamas control following an October 2025 ceasefire.
An AFP journalist reported seeing Israeli tanks positioning themselves east of the Nuseirat refugee camp.
Hamas denounced a "blatant ceasefire violation," while the military said the rare ground incursion was a response to Hamas ceasefire violations in the area.
The military said in a statement that the operation had been launched to "dismantle a terror tunnel west of the Yellow Line that posed an immediate and direct threat to IDF troops".

A Gaza security source told AFP there had been "intense Israeli artillery shelling" north of Nuseirat refugee camp and reported Israeli military vehicles in central Gaza "amid ongoing gunfire and airstrikes since midday".
Israel and Hamas regularly accuse each other of violating the U.S.-brokered ceasefire deal that came after two years of devastating war sparked by Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack on Israel.

More than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the start of the ceasefire, according to an AFP tally based on data from the Gaza Health Ministry, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.
Over the same period, the Israeli military says seven of its soldiers have been killed, as well as one civilian contractor.

articles.title: COP31 negotiators publish revised deal draft with no mention of fossil fuels
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The revised deal, ‌which is not expected to be the final version, was weaker on some of the conference's central topics — fossil fuels, electrification and adaptation finance — compared to a first draft ‌published on November 16

Climate negotiators stripped out any reference to ‌ending the use of fossil fuels in a slimmed-down draft deal text published ​on Thursday (November 19, 2026), as the COP31 meeting in Antalya, Turkiye, approaches its Friday (November 20, 2026) deadline.

The talks are ⁠taking place at a time when war and rising living costs are competing for the attention of policymakers and the public against the warming climate and its increasingly severe effects, including heatwaves, floods and droughts.

The revised deal, ‌which is not expected to be the final version, was weaker on some of the conference's central topics — fossil fuels, electrification and adaptation finance — compared to a first draft ‌published on Monday (November 16, 2026).

Monday's (November 16, 2026) two references to fossil fuels and limiting their use — a topic that ‌deeply ⁠divides nations in the negotiations every year — were removed, as was mention of a $120 ⁠billion target for finance to help developing countries adapt to climate change.
"This new text has gone backwards from the one released earlier in the week," said Mohamed Adow, director of climate and energy think tank Power Shift Africa.
"If this version of ​the text remains, it will be a ‌ghost COP. The summit will have nothing to show for what happened here."

Thursday's (November 19, 2026) draft did retain an acknowledgement that global warming could exceed the 1.5 degrees Celsius threshold countries have sought to preserve, and the need for "deep, rapid and sustained" cuts to greenhouse gas emissions.
It also encouraged efforts ‌to scale up the deployment of technologies that can suck carbon out of the atmosphere, something ​scientists say would be needed to bring temperatures back down.

Australia, which is leading negotiations under a split presidency arrangement with Turkiye, previously ⁠said Monday's (November 16, 2026) opening draft of the deal was always intended to be a broad document that would then be narrowed down.

While the conference is scheduled to end on Friday (November 20, 2026), in recent years, efforts to secure ‌consensus among the nearly 200 countries participating have regularly blown past this deadline by more than 24 hours.
The need to limit rising global temperatures is widely accepted by participants, but they don't all agree on the best way to do so, who should pay for it, and how quickly the world needs to act.

Thursday's (November 19, 2026) draft deal also called for "global cooperation" to boost electricity’s share of world energy consumption to 35% by 2035, up from around 23% now — something proponents say would slash greenhouse gas emissions ‌by reducing fossil fuel use.

articles.title: Third Ukrainian strike in 4 days halts rail traffic on Russia's Kerch Bridge to Crimea
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The attack came hours before the start of talks in Berlin between U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy alongside more than 40 European leaders who are supporting Ukraine's war effort

A third Ukrainian aerial attack in four days on the key Kerch Bridge linking Russia to Russian-held Crimea halted rail traffic across the span, officials said Thursday (November 19, 2026), after earlier strikes shut down the road section of the landmark that is a symbol of Moscow's invasion.
Train traffic across the bridge stopped after the overnight strike while authorities assessed the damage, but it resumed in the afternoon, according to Russian state news agency RIA Novosti .

The Ukrainian strikes seemed calculated to embarrass Russian President Vladimir Putin as he met in China with President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump, as well as to demonstrate that Kyiv still holds cards in the war and to undermine Russia's argument that its victory is inevitable.

The attack came hours before the start of talks in Berlin between U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy alongside more than 40 European leaders who are supporting Ukraine's war effort and fear being sidelined by Mr. Trump's direct talks with Mr. Putin.
“We will respond to these attacks, and I want everyone to be clear about that,” Mr. Putin told reporters in Shenzhen, China.
He insisted the bridge is a civilian asset, adding that he had ordered the bridge closed to the transport of military hardware or ammunition.
Mr. Putin also said that the road side of the bridge had been “seriously damaged” but vowed to rebuild it.
The rail section is believed to be stronger than the road side, to bear the greater weight of cargo wagons.

The 19-kilometre (12-mile) Kerch Bridge is a key route for military and civilian supplies to Crimea, which Moscow seized in defiance of international law in 2014 and uses to support front-line troops. It is a potent reminder of Russia's illegal annexation of the territory and has been a prime target for Ukraine.

A large section of the road deck and an arch collapsed in the culmination of weeks of preparatory strikes over seven stages of the operation, according to Mr. Zelenskyy, and the train track was damaged by domestically produced Neptune missiles, Ukraine's Defence Ministry said.
Now Russia will need to reroute fuel and ammunition supplies over land, where “our drones are waiting for the cargo,” the ministry said.
The Russian Defence Ministry said on Thursday (November 19, 2026) that its air defences intercepted 53 Ukrainian drones over 10 Russian regions during the night.

articles.title: How U.S. controls flow of advanced tech, chip, and compute to China | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The U.S. Commerce Department, on November 16, 2026, issued an interim final rule barring data centre operators outside of the U.S., equipped with advanced American AI chips, from providing cloud service to businesses in two dozen countries, including China, Iran and Russia

The story so far: The battle for the most sought after commodity that underpins development of artificial intelligence technology just grew fiercer after the U.S. Commerce Department, on November 16, 2026, issued an interim final rule (IFR) barring data centre operators outside of the U.S., equipped with advanced American AI chips, from providing cloud service to businesses in two dozen countries, including China, Iran and Russia. The new, yet to be published, rule also restricts American companies from freely shipping high-end AI chips to a set of five countries, including Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore, without the explicit approval of the U.S. government.

China has censured the move, calling it “yet another case of the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security, and abusing export control measures to interfere in normal trade and tech cooperation between China and other countries and go after China’s high-tech industry.”
The interim rule came just days ahead of the meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and China’s President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China on the sidelines of the November 18-19 APEC Summit.

The U.S. government’s policy on making advanced technology inaccessible to China has been a talking point among lawmakers in Washington for well over a decade, but a legal tool to control the flow took shape only during the first Trump term when the administration passed the Export Control Reform Act in 2018.

It gave the U.S. a legal weapon to control the movement of advanced technology originating from the country. Its primary purpose was to curb export of top-tier chips that had dual-use — both commercial and military purposes — to countries like China, Russia and Iran.

• The U.S. Commerce Department, on November 16, 2026, issued an interim final rule barring data centre operators outside of the U.S., equipped with advanced American AI chips, from providing cloud service to businesses in two dozen countries, including China, Iran and Russia
• The story so far: The battle for the most sought after commodity that underpins development of artificial intelligence technology just grew fiercer after the U.S. Commerce Department, on November 16, 2026, issued an interim final rule (IFR) barring data centre operators outside of the U.S., equipped with advanced American AI chips, from providing cloud service to businesses in two dozen countries, including China, Iran and Russia. The new, yet to be published, rule also restricts American companies from freely shipping high-end AI chips to a set of five countries, including Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore, without the explicit approval of the U.S. government.
• China has censured the move, calling it “yet another case of the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security, and abusing export control measures to interfere in normal trade and tech cooperation between China and other countries and go after China’s high-tech industry.”

articles.title: Why data interoperability is critical to the future of hospital care
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The future of critical care will be defined by how effectively the information is connected, interpreted and applied

In an intensive care unit, every second matters. A critically ill patient may be connected to several devices, including patient monitors, ventilators and infusion pumps, while laboratory systems and electronic health records continuously generate additional information. Together, these systems create a large and rapidly-changing picture of the patient’s condition. However, when the information remains fragmented across devices and platforms, clinicians may spend valuable time locating, verifying and reconciling data before they can act.

This makes interoperability a clinical priority in critical care, not simply an information technology requirement. Integration enables systems to exchange data, but true interoperability ensures that the information being exchanged is accurate, interpretable and clinically relevant. This can help care teams coordinate and prioritise interventions more effectively while reducing the need to move between multiple systems to assemble a clinical picture.

articles.title: Elusive peace: On Kashmir terror attack
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Restoration of Statehood is essential for peace in Jammu and Kashmir

Three months of lull established by security forces in Jammu and Kashmir was rattled by the back-to-back incidents of violence in the past six days. On November 11, a terror attack on a checkpoint manned by the personnel of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) in Kulgam left three jawans injured. On November 16, a local, whom the police suspected of having joined the terror ranks a few days ago, was killed after six days of a siege-like anti-terror operation in residential areas of Kulgam. In Jammu’s Kishtwar, two Special Police Officers (SPOs) of the J&K Police were found dead with bullet wounds, a day after they were reported missing in a forest range on November 11. The police and the Army, however, remain tight-lipped about the circumstances around the killing of these SPOs, and there are conflicting reports on the circumstances that led to their deaths. The anti-terror operation in civilian areas of Kulgam has raised concerns. Former J&K Chief Minister and PDP president Mehbooba Mufti described the operation, spread over six days, as “collective punishment that only breeds alienation and resentment,” while NC spokesman Imran Nabi Dar suggested that entire villages were put under prolonged restrictions for days. The Omar Abdullah government , because of limited powers and no jurisdiction over the police in J&K, a Union Territory since 2019, finds itself hamstrung. The iron hand policy to stamp out terrorism and separatism has been effective from a strictly security perspective — terror attacks as well as local recruitments into terror ranks have declined. According to the police, local recruits have come down to single digit or fewer than 10 in Kashmir.

That said, the decline in terrorist incidents and the silence of the streets should not be mistaken for peace. The current situation demands a political reach-out by the Centre to all the stakeholders of J&K. It has to begin with the much-promised restoration of Statehood , which will give the voters a sense that their mass participation in the 2024 Assembly elections allowed their elected leaders to hold institutions accountable, and they were able to work freely to protect the interests of the region. Though the security agencies need to be focused on Pakistan-backed terrorism, it should not come at the cost of re-inflicting psychological scars within Kashmir, which could turn into a powder keg if left unattended. Healing through both political and security processes has to be complementary rather than conflicting. Allowing the political class of J&K to establish its writ and providing room to security agencies to combat challenges are not contradictory.
Editorial Context: Elusive peace: On Kashmir terror attack. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and administrative dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: A step back: On Trump’s no-war, no-deal approach against Iran
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Trump must accept the realities of the war if he wants a deal

Before the November 3 midterm elections, U.S. President Donald Trump had repeatedly threatened to “destroy” Iran unless it entered into a deal with the U.S. to end the war. Since the elections, in which Mr. Trump’s Republican Party suffered a massive defeat , the U.S. President appears to have toned down his rhetoric. Last week, he said he had decided against escalating the military conflict with Iran following requests from America’s Gulf allies. But the U.S. would maintain the naval blockade of the Islamic Republic. Mr. Trump also pulled Vice President J.D. Vance off negotiations with Iran, as the Qatar-mediated talks made no real progress. Iran wants the U.S. to lift the blockade, unfreeze its frozen assets, issue sanctions relief and pull back from the Persian Gulf for direct negotiations on the nuclear programme to restart. The U.S., which calls Iran’s demands “outrageous”, has now adopted a no-war, no-deal approach , hoping that the economic blockade would force Tehran to offer concessions in the near future. Mr. Trump’s retreat from the threats reflects the realities on the ground. Before the U.S. and Israel launched this war by assassinating Iran’s Supreme Leader on February 28, Tehran was ready to make concessions. The U.S. and Israel carried out heavy bombing for 40 days but achieved none of their declared objectives. There is no guarantee that another round of strikes would force Iran to change its position. And the war, as the midterm results show, remains very unpopular in America.

Mr. Trump has only himself, and Benjamin Netanyahu, to blame for the predicament he is in. He is the one who sabotaged a functioning Obama-era nuclear deal in 2018 that had denied Iran a path towards the nuclear bomb. Mr. Trump joined Israel’s unprovoked war on Iran in June 2025 and declared that he had “obliterated” Iran’s nuclear programme. And the same Mr. Trump started the current war, just eight months later, over the same nuclear programme. The Iranian state has survived, though Iranians are facing enormous economic woes. Tehran shut the Strait of Hormuz, pumping up global energy prices. Iran’s counterattacks have either destroyed or damaged America’s bases in the Persian Gulf. High oil prices and inflation turned the American electorate against the Republican party, while in Israel, Mr. Netanyahu, despite war rhetoric and racist attacks on the country’s Arab minorities, lost the governing majority. The setbacks are there for anyone to see. Yet, Mr. Trump does not seem to have grasped the seriousness of the situation. His no-war, no-deal approach r isks a resumption of hostilities as Iran has pledged to break the siege. The U.S. has few clear military options unless it is prepared to launch a ground invasion, which would be disastrous. A more rational way forward is to end the war through diplomacy. But for that, Mr. Trump must first accept the strategic reality that he has lost the war.

articles.title: Stoop to conquer: On the Opposition’s seat-sharing ahead of U.P. polls
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The Congress should scale down its ambition while seeking an alliance with the SP

As Uttar Pradesh heads to the polls in early 2027, a familiar seat-sharing tussle has emerged within the Opposition. articles.title: Ruckus erupts between SFI activists and police over setting up bookstalls near Calcutta University
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The SFI leaders said they sought permission from the Kolkata Police to set up a bookstall on the College Street footpath, but police refused on November 16 evening, saying it could disrupt traffic

A ruckus erupted between supporters of the Students’ Federation of India (SFI), the student wing of the Communist Party of India (Marxist), and police near the University of Kolkata for setting up a book stall. After the clash, police detained several SFI supporters, including the SFI State secretary, Debanjan Dey.

The SFI leadership said that they sought permission from the Kolkata Police to set up a book stall at a makeshift stall on the footpath of College Street. However, the police refused to grant permission on Monday evening, stating that it might disrupt traffic. The book stall was part of a three-day campaign, “Sangrami Boipotro”, by the party. It was supposed to be inaugurated by the Left Front chairman, Biman Bose, on Tuesday evening.

“We have permission from the Kolkata Municipal Corporation and Jorasanko Police Station for a period of five years to set up bookstalls at College Street. Necessary tax was also paid to the concerned authorities. We have been setting up such stalls for the last four years. Our plan was to do the same this year too. But the Kolkata Police have now refused to allow us anymore,” said Mr. Dey to the media persons

The protesters said that a few police vans had already been stationed on College Street since Monday night. When they began preparing to set up the stalls on Tuesday morning, the police stopped them and said that no book stalls could be organised in the area.

The situation escalated when they blocked College Street and staged a sit-in. They laid out a sheet on the tram line in the middle of the road and began selling their books. They also invited the police to buy books for their children. It immediately resulted in a clash with the police. The police were seen using mild force to disrupt the protesters and clear the road. Several activists, including Mr. Dey, Subhadeep Bandyopadhyay, Didhiti Roy, and Haseeb Hossain, have been detained.

“A heavy police force was deployed across College Street on Tuesday only to stop us selling some books. They have assaulted the students who have been fighting for the books. It is now clear that the government has declared war against the books. They want to destroy the culture and tradition of Bengal. We will have to fight the battle with books only against them,” said Mr. Dey after the detention.
Following the development, the left student union also organised a rally in the evening at the Mahabodhi Society and demanded the immediate release of the detained students.

The dispute over the book stalls set up by the Left parties began during Durga Puja. Police and civic bodies demolished several stalls set up by the parties across Kolkata. In Jadavpur, a bulldozer was also brought in to dismantle a stall, sparking a huge political controversy. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari had described Left party supporters as “atheist” and declared that they would not be allowed to set up their book stalls near puja pandals, where such stalls have been a fixture for decades.

articles.title: Convocation ceremony row: Maharaja’s College council asks suspended students to accept their mistake
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The incident caused disrepute to the image of the institution in the public domain, finds inquiry report

A meeting of the council of Maharaja’s College, Kochi, held on Tuesday accepted an inquiry committee report that indicted activists of the Students’ Federation of India (SFI) for disrupting a convocation ceremony attended by Minister for Higher Education Roji M. John on October 30.

The meeting recommended that V. Praneel Raj, chairperson, and Nafeesathul Misriya, vice-chairperson of the college union, who were suspended in connection with the incident on November 2, submit an apology admitting their mistake. The inquiry committee report found that the incident had caused disrepute to the image of the institution in the public domain, according to sources.

The council observed that it did not wish to initiate further disciplinary action against the students, but they need to accept their mistake. The meeting took note of the case registered by the police against 10 SFI activists booked in connection with the protest.

SFI activists staged the protest soon after the Minister completed his inaugural address at the convocation ceremony, seeking answers from him on the suspension of 16 students of Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit, Kalady. The activists demanded that the Minister withdraw his alleged statements against those who were suspended for protesting against Vice-Chancellor Ciza Thomas. Following the protest, Mr. John had to leave the function midway.

fullParagraphs: The complainant, a resident of Mulavukad, was allegedly cheated by an unidentified person who contacted her over the phone, promising to activate a credit card issued by a private sector bank
The Kochi City cyber police have registered a case after a 36-year-old woman was allegedly cheated of nearly ₹90,000 on the pretext of activating a credit card.

The complainant, a resident of Mulavukad, was allegedly cheated by an unidentified person who contacted her over the phone, promising to activate a credit card issued by a private sector bank. On November 2, the accused convinced her to share a one-time password (OTP) to activate the card using another credit card she owns. She lost ₹49,440 after sharing the OTP. Two days later, the accused contacted the woman again and asked her to share another OTP to credit the amount debited earlier back to her card. This time, she was duped of ₹40,464.
The police have registered a case of cheating under Section 318 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

articles.title: Kerala High Court allows Cusat employees to seek review of suspension
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The court directed the Syndicate to examine whether the continued suspension was justified
The Kerala High Court has held that the suspended employees of the Cochin University of Science and Technology (Cusat) can approach the university Syndicate seeking a review of their suspension.

Justice P. Gopinath issued the interim direction in view of the Syndicate meeting scheduled for November 21. The court directed the Syndicate to examine whether the continued suspension was justified. It also instructed the petitioners to file an application before the Syndicate seeking a review of the suspension order.
Cusat Employees Association members Anurin Salim, P.M. Sivadas, and Harilal had approached the court challenging the suspension order.

The Syndicate had suspended the petitioners based on an inquiry report by the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) into allegations of irregularities in appointments to the sweeper-cum-cleaner posts. They alleged that the officials were not given an opportunity to explain their position and that they were suspended before a charge memo was issued.

articles.title: Opposition, ruling councillors in Keralam’s Kochi Corporation spar over Thuruthy Towers, ro-ro service at stormy council meet
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: LDF seeks dates for apartment handover and launch of third ro-ro vessel; UDF cites procedural delays in commissioning vessel; Opposition alleges UDF is using losses incurred by KSINC to justify privatisation of ro-ro ferry operations

The Opposition Left Democratic Front (LDF) staged a protest towards the fag end of the Kochi Corporation council meeting on Tuesday, disrupting proceedings over the alleged delay in handing over apartments to beneficiaries of Thuruthy Towers in the Kalvathy division and the induction of the third roll-on roll-off (ro-ro) vessel into service. The Opposition demanded that dates for both be announced in the council.

LDF councillors sought to know why the new vessel was yet to commence operations despite being inaugurated by Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on July 12. They also accused the ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) council of attempting to pave the way for the privatisation of ro-ro operations by highlighting losses incurred by the existing public sector operator, Kerala Shipping and Inland Navigation Corporation Limited (KSINC).

LDF councillor P.J. Yesudas drew attention to the hardships faced by commuters on the Fort Kochi-Vypeen route, as one of the two existing ro-ro vessels has remained out of service for the past five days due to a snag. “Though the Mayor announced the formation of a sub-committee to discuss issues affecting the ro-ro service, it has not met even once. The new vessel should be introduced without further delay ahead of the festive season in December, when lakhs visit Fort Kochi for the Carnival and New Year celebrations. Any further delay runs the risk of a tragedy similar to the Fort Kochi boat accident 11 years ago,” he said.

UDF councillor Henry Austin attributed the delay to the formation of the special purpose vehicle (SPV) to manage ro-ro services and the time taken to secure nearly 10 different certificates and licences before commissioning the vessel. “We cannot afford inadequacies in the formation of the SPV as it would ultimately cost the Corporation. There is no need to create a narrative that the service is being run at a loss to justify privatisation, since it has been operating at a loss from the very outset,” he said.

Welfare standing committee chairperson Antony Painuthara said the SPV had been formed and would be placed before the council for approval on Wednesday, following which it would be submitted to the government for clearance. He said the UDF council had managed to constitute the SPV within a year, whereas the LDF had failed to do so despite being in power in the Corporation for five years. He also questioned how the new vessel, ordered during the previous council’s tenure, had cost ₹15 crore, while the two vessels introduced during the LDF administration had collectively cost ₹10 crore.

LDF parliamentary party leader V.A. Sreejith alleged that the council was being repeatedly misled, citing multiple missed deadlines for handing over the Thuruthy apartments, the latest being November 1. “The lack of clarity in the beneficiary list is being cited as the reason for the delay, though the welfare standing committee met thrice to resolve the issue. The list has also not been placed before the council. The apartments should be handed over immediately to eligible beneficiaries who have completed all formalities, followed by the rest at the earliest,” he said.

Works standing committee chairperson T.K. Asharaf initially said the apartments would be handed over in December, but later claimed that letters had been sent to more than 250 beneficiaries informing them that the apartments were ready for occupancy. The LDF then sought clarification from the Corporation secretary, who said the council would be updated on Wednesday. The Opposition also rejected the UDF’s allegation that the towers had been inaugurated by the former Chief Minister before the completion of the works, pointing out that 24 storeys had been constructed during the previous council’s tenure.

articles.title: Earthshot Prize: Climate action needs innovation, global cooperation, say leaders on green carpet in Mumbai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Maharashtra Environment and Climate Change Minister Pankaja Munde called for global cooperation to protect the planet for future generations

Global leaders, business executives, and celebrities called for greater investment in environmental innovations and collective action against climate change as they gathered on the green carpet ahead of the Earthshot Prize Awards in Mumbai on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).
Among those attending were former New Zealand Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern, Serum Institute of India CEO Adar Poonawalla, filmmaker Karan Johar, and Maharashtra Environment Minister Pankaja Mund.
Speaking to reporters, Mr. Poonawalla emphasised the importance of supporting environmental innovations and helping them attract investment.

“Prevention is better than cure—that’s what we believe at Serum Institute,” he said, explaining the company’s partnership with the Earthshot Prize. He added that the initiative would help innovators connect with investors and scale up technologies capable of addressing environmental challenges.
Ms. Ardern welcomed the awards to Mumbai, highlighting India’s record of producing the highest number of Earthshot finalists and winners.

“The Earthshot Prize is showcasing responses to that crisis to demonstrate that things are happening and innovation is available, we just need to scale it up with speed,” she said, referring to the climate crisis.

Coral Pasisi, president of Tofia, Niue, highlighted Indigenous-led ocean conservation efforts. “We’re protecting one of the largest areas of ocean on the planet. And we developed a sustainable financing mechanism that’s driven by Indigenous people,” she said, stressing the need for international support.

Maharashtra Environment and Climate Change Minister Pankaja Munde called for global cooperation to protect the planet for future generations. She expressed concern that rapid urbanisation and industrialisation had drowned out natural sounds, including birdsong and flowing water, and urged people to protect forests and biodiversity.
Filmmaker Karan Johar praised Prince William’s environmental commitment, describing him as a “climate warrior” who empowered innovators through the Earthshot Prize.

Actor Sonam Kapoor emphasised that environmental responsibility extended beyond public statements. Speaking about her children, she said individuals and governments needed to take concrete steps to protect the environment for future generations.

Former Indian football captain Sunil Chhetri, attending with Football for Peace for its “Rehydrate the Earth” campaign, stressed the importance of awareness and collective efforts to minimise environmental risks.

Founded by Prince William, the Earthshot Prize recognises innovative solutions to environmental challenges, including climate change, pollution, biodiversity loss and ocean conservation. Five winners are selected annually, each receiving £1 million to help scale their solutions.

articles.title: Fearmongering around fake drugs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: As per the last National Drug Survey published in 2017, the volume of counterfeit drugs in the Indian market detected in the survey was at a negligible 0.0245%

Recent news from Karnataka regarding the seizure of fake cancer drugs from a licensed distributor during a raid has understandably sparked concerns. Counterfeit drugs for serious conditions like cancer are a sensational and emotive issue, often provoking a demand for severe action, including death sentences for those involved in the distribution.

However, in this case, there is a serious reason to doubt the authenticity of the news reports about the recent seizure since the Government of Karnataka has not confirmed that indeed counterfeit cancer drugs were seized in the raid. While a purported list of the drugs seized was circulated on social media, it only contained antibiotics, not cancer drugs. The silence of the State Health Department on the news reports about the counterfeit drugs is insensitive to the dread and uncertainty being faced by patients receiving cancer treatment, not to mention the doubts of those wondering whether they lost their loved ones to cancer because of counterfeit drugs. The Department should clear the air on the matter by issuing a press release or holding a press conference. If counterfeit cancer drugs were indeed seized, the government should release the names of the drugs and the hospitals possibly affected. If not, it should at least communicate the same to the public. Letting the uncertainty hang without authoritative answers is not in public interest.

articles.title: Transgender rights, healthcare should not be compromised
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Clinical understanding of the care needs of a transgender person remains rudimentary in India. Doctors, nurses, receptionists, security staff and hospital administrators need to be trained in basic transgender health.

Parliament passed the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, 2026 earlier this year. The new Act represents a significant shift from the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019. The 2026 amendment removes the principle of self-identification and demands a medical board’s recommendation; a selection from prescribed categories; and certification by a District Magistrate. It fundamentally changes legal recognition for transgender persons from self-identification to medical assessment. While the 2026 Act does increase protection, it changes the philosophical foundation of transgender rights — from recognition based substantially on autonomy and self-identification towards recognition mediated by medical and administrative authorities.

The definition of “transgender” as introduced in the Amendment Act is in contradiction to established international evidence and guidelines laid down in the World Health Organization ICD-11 and the World Professional Association for Transgender Health Standards of Care Version 8.

articles.title: Prince William says Gen Z is the torchbearer of the global movement for change
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Himalayan Kingdom of Bhutan, Mahindra Last Mile Mobility among the five winners of Earthshot Prize

Young people from around the world are not waiting for someone else to find the solution, they are the torchbearers of the global movement for change, Britain’s Prince William said in Mumbai on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).
He was speaking at the 2026 Earthshot Prize Awards Ceremony, which was held in India for the first time.

“India is a nation of extraordinary innovation, ambition, facing immense environmental pressures, yet moving ahead with determination. Not because the challenge is simple, not because the path is easy. But because millions of people have decided that progress simply cannot wait,” said Prince William.
Winners of the Earthshot Prize award were declared under five categories in a glittering ceremony. The awardees include the Himalayan Kingdom of Bhutan and Mahindra Last Mile Mobility.
“They [Gen Z] are bringing fresh ideas and showing what is possible when optimism is matched with action. Their ideas, their energy, and their determination are helping to shape the future,” he said.
During his address, Prince William reflected on the achievements of this year’s finalists and the growing global movement behind environmental innovation.
The ceremony was attended by environmental innovators, philanthropists, business leaders, government representatives and global figures from sport, entertainment and culture.
Mahindra Last Mile Mobility won the Earthshot Prize in the ‘Clean Our Air’ category. Accepting the award, the company’s CEO, Suman Mishra, said it showed how urgent optimism worked.
The company has won 1 million pounds for its efforts, due to which 33 per cent of India’s three-wheelers are now electric.
Prince Williams and Princess Catherine meet the winners of Earthshot Prize post the award ceremony in Mumbai on November 17, 2026. | Photo Credit: Emmanual Yogini
In the ‘Revive Our Oceans’ category, Niue Ocean Wide Trust was chosen for protecting the oceans, especially the vast Pacific region.
Coral Pasisi, vice chair and co-architect of Ocean Conservation Commitments, expressed gratitude for indigenous, people-led sustainability efforts being honoured.

articles.title: Kedarnath generates 73 tonnes of waste during 2026 Char Dham Yatra
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Around 65.65 lakh pilgrims visit four Char Dham shrines and Hemkund Sahib in 2026 as Badrinath portals close for winter

Pilgrims visiting the Kedarnath shrine generated 73 tonnes of waste during the 2026 Char Dham Yatra, more than three times the amount recorded last year. The yatra, which ended on Monday (November 16, 2026) with the closure of the Badrinath shrine portals, witnessed a record 65.65 lakh pilgrims this year.
According to data shared by the civic body at Kedarnath, the 73 tonnes of waste comprised plastic bottles, food packets, Tetra Pak, and cardboard.
Neeraj Kukreti, an official of the Kedarnath Nagar Panchayat, told The Hindu that waste generation this year was more than three times the 21.40 tonnes recorded in 2025.
The waste generated in Kedarnath stood at 26.10 tonnes in 2024 and 32.58 tonnes in 2023, he added.

To help manage the waste buildup near the temple, the district administration launched the ‘Carry Me Back’ initiative in June. The drive mobilised over 6,000 pilgrims to carry 14 tonnes of waste down to a collection point, from where it was sent for segregation and disposal.”

The increase in waste generation comes amid a broader rise in pilgrim numbers across Uttarakhand’s Char Dham circuit, according to a comparative analysis released by the Dehradun-based SDC Foundation.

Prepared by Anoop Nautiyal and Praveen Upreti, the study found that 65.65 lakh pilgrims visited the four Char Dham shrines — Kedarnath, Badrinath, Gangotri and Yamunotri — and Hemkund Sahib in 2026, registering a 29% increase over 51.07 lakh in 2025. The pilgrimage season extended from mid-April to mid-November.

Kedarnath recorded 19,33,138 pilgrims, a 9% rise over the previous year. However, its average daily footfall declined by around 6%, from 10,113 pilgrims in 2025 to 9,476 in 2026. The foundation attributed the higher cumulative numbers partly to a longer pilgrimage season and fewer weather-related disruptions. Kedarnath remained operational for 204 days, compared with 175 days last year.

The SDC Foundation report also flagged concerns over pilgrim safety, recording 297 fatalities across the five shrines in 2026, compared with 182 in 2025. Health-related natural deaths alone increased by 81%, from 159 to 288, with Kedarnath accounting for 142 such deaths.

Vehicle movement during the Char Dham Yatra also witnessed a significant rise, increasing from 5,14,016 in 2025 to 6,68,877 in 2026 (till November 14). This represents an increase of 1,54,861 vehicles, or more than 30% over the previous year.

“The sharp rise in vehicle numbers reflects the growing pressure on pilgrimage infrastructure, road networks, traffic management, road safety and healthcare services. These trends underline the urgent need for strengthened safety measures, improved traffic management and a more coordinated, data-driven approach to ensuring a safe and sustainable Char Dham Yatra,” said Mr. Nautiyal.

He stressed that Uttarakhand must move beyond the pursuit of record-breaking pilgrim numbers and focus on carrying capacity, pilgrim health, sustainability and the long-term future of the Char Dham Yatra.

articles.title: Won’t allow hiring of outsiders, hire locals: J&K CM Omar Abdullah to outside companies
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: He made the statement during the inauguration of development projects worth ₹30 crores in Jammu, Samba and Kathua districts
Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) said that companies from the outside must hire locals and that hiring outsiders will not be allowed.

“The excuse that trained youths are not available will not work. We will provide you (companies) six months or one year and prepare our youths. We also have ITIs (Industrial Training Institutes), polytechnics, colleges, and universities,” said Mr. Abdullah.
The J&K Chief Minister said youths from J&K have no shortage of talent. “They (youths) only need opportunities. We will not tolerate excuses at the cost of our children’s future,” said Mr. Abdullah.
He made the statement during the inauguration of development projects worth ₹30 crores in Jammu, Samba and Kathua districts.

articles.title: Jharkhand SIR: Final BLO meetings at poll stations on November 18
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Jharkhand CEO K Ravi Kumar appeals to all eligible Indian citizens in the state to ensure their names are included in the electoral roll by taking part in Ek Aur Avsar (One More Opportunity) camps

Jharkhand Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) K. Ravi Kumar on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) appealed to all eligible Indian citizens in the State to ensure their names are included in the electoral roll being published under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).

Speaking to the media in Ranchi, Mr. Ravi asserted that an “Ek Aur Avsar” (One More Opportunity) camp will be held on November 18 at all polling stations in the State, from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., where meetings of BLOs (Booth Level Officers) and BLAs-2 (Booth Level Agents-2) will take place in the form of a “Chunav Pathshala” (Electoral Awareness Session).

He pointed out that the objective of this special initiative is to provide one additional opportunity for any eligible Indian citizen who, for various reasons, has not yet had their name added to the electoral roll.

Mr. Ravi explained that the camps will focus primarily on three key areas. First, the Election Commission of India (ECI) is republishing the ASDD (Absent, Shifted, Dead, or Duplicate) list at all polling stations. If any eligible Indian citizen has been included in this list, they may follow the prescribed procedure to submit Form-6 or an enumeration form.

Second, lists of voters in categories such as “No Mapping” or those with “Logical Discrepancies”—who have failed to provide the necessary documentation despite receiving two notices from the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) and undergoing a door-to-door verification process—will be made available at the respective polling stations.

Third, efforts are being made to identify eligible Indian citizens who will have turned 18 by October 1, 2026, but who have not yet registered their names in the electoral roll for their respective polling stations. Eligible Indian citizens will be able to have their names included in the electoral roll by submitting Form 6.

The CEO said that this is the sixth and final BLO-BLA-2 meeting being held under the ongoing SIR process in Jharkhand. He urged all eligible citizens in the state to take advantage of this opportunity and get their names added to the electoral roll, ensuring that no eligible Indian citizen remains excluded.

The ECI has already extended the deadline for final publication of electoral rolls in Jharkhand under the SIR to November 30. The final publication was initially scheduled for October 7 and was later extended to October 19 before being revised.

articles.title: Construction activities on Kaziranga wildlife corridors flagged
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: An Eastern Assam-based environment activist writes to the Supreme Court-constituted Central Empowered Committee, highlighting the concerns

An eastern Assam-based environmental activist has reminded the Supreme Court–constituted Central Empowered Committee (CEC) to continue construction activities on the wildlife corridors of Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve.

Kaziranga has nine notified wildlife corridors and several dandis or animal pathways. Animals use these corridors and dandis mostly to escape to the hills of Karbi Anglong district when the park is flooded during the monsoon months.

In a letter to the CEC’s Member-Secretary on November 16, Rohit Choudhury said he had brought such construction activities to the notice of the Committee on May 11. He lamented the lack of action against these activities, violating the Supreme Court’s April 2019 order.

“We order that all kinds of mining and related activities along the aforesaid Kaziranga National Park area and in the entire catchment area of rivers, streams and rivulets originating in the Karbi Anglong Hill ranges and flowing into Kaziranga National Park, including the Tiger Reserve, are restrained. No new construction shall be permitted on private lands which form part of the nine identified animal corridors,” the apex court’s order read.

“Despite this clear and categorical prohibition, the Government of Assam has displayed a disturbing disregard for the mandate of the Supreme Court by permitting and facilitating unlawful construction activities within these ecologically sensitive wildlife corridors,” Mr. Choudhury wrote.

He reminded the CEC of photographic evidence of a building under construction on the Haldhibari Wildlife Corridor attached to his May 11 letter. “The construction activity was allowed to proceed unabated and has now reached an advanced stage of completion,” he wrote, attaching recent photographs of the construction site.

Mr. Choudhury said the CEC’s inability to take up the matter six months ago “effectively afforded the concerned authorities sufficient time to continue and substantially complete the illegal construction”.
He said such delays in addressing matters of grave environmental significance seriously undermine the purpose and efficacy of the CEC’s mandate.
The activist further said the Assam Government did not inform the Supreme Court of any instance of violation of its April 12, 2019, order for necessary action.

“This persistent failure of enforcement has emboldened continued violations and weakened the protection envisaged by the Supreme Court,” he said, urging the CEC to recommend contempt proceedings against the officials responsible for permitting, facilitating or failing to prevent these blatant violations of the court’s binding directions.

“The matter concerns not merely a breach of judicial orders but the continued degradation of one of India’s most treasured ecological landscapes and a globally recognised natural heritage site. Immediate intervention is therefore both necessary and imperative,” Mr. Choudhury wrote.

articles.title: Russian military transport plane crashes in Siberia, killing 19: Defence Ministry
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The An-12 aircraft went down in an unpopulated area near the city of Kemerovo, about 3,000 kilometres (about 1,860 miles) east of Moscow

A Russian military transport plane crashed in western Siberia on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), killing all 19 people on board, the Defence Ministry said. Preliminary findings pointed to equipment failure.

The An-12 aircraft went down in an unpopulated area near the city of Kemerovo, about 3,000 kilometres (about 1,860 miles) east of Moscow. Air force experts were investigating the cause of the crash. The An-12 typically has a crew of six.
Kemerovo Gov. Ilya Serdyuk said the plane crashed near the village of Yagunovo, which is close to Kemerovo airport. “Emergency responders put out a fire on the site of the crash,” he said.
The Investigative Committee, the country’s top criminal investigation agency, launched an inquiry into possible violations of flight safety rules, a standard practice following crashes.
The An-12 is a Soviet-built four-engine turboprop transport plane that has been in service since the late 1950s. Over 1,000 were built and some still remain in operation in Russia and other nations.

articles.title: U.K. hands NATO-assigned American soldier accused of Russia spying to U.S.
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: A U.S. Army official has named the detained soldier as 41-year-old Lieutenant Colonel Brandon Tyner

A senior American soldier assigned to NATO who was arrested in Britain last week on suspicion of spying for Russia has been transferred to U.S. military custody, U.K. police said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

The espionage case, the latest involving suspected Kremlin agents in Britain and elsewhere in Europe, comes amid heightened tensions between Moscow and various European capitals after Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
It also follows recent security scares at two British air force bases hosting the U.S. military, with officials accusing Iran of involvement in plots to target them.
A U.S. Army official has named the detained soldier as 41-year-old Lieutenant Colonel Brandon Tyner.

Held in British police custody since his November 10 arrest near Gloucester, southwest England, he was handed to the US military “over suspected national security and espionage allegations”, U.K. Counter Terrorism Policing said.

Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor said the decision to “pass the investigation to them to progress” followed an extensive probe by his counter-terror unit and subsequent discussions between British prosecutors and “American partners”.
FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement that the unnamed Army officer was in U.S. custody after “an espionage investigation”.
He noted it had involved “close cooperation” between the FBI’s Philadelphia field office and various other US and UK law enforcement and intelligence agencies.
“Together we worked to identify a potential threat to national security and take swift action,” Mr. Patel added.

A senior NATO military official last week confirmed that the arrested soldier had been assigned to its Allied Rapid Reaction Corps (ARRC), the alliance’s 20-nation, high-readiness force led by the British Army.
Based at Imjin Barracks near Gloucester, it can deploy at short notice anywhere in Europe or globally under the direct operational command of NATO’s Supreme Allied Commander Europe.
Imjin is also just a few miles from the U.K.’s highly sensitive GCHQ intelligence, security and cyber agency headquarters.

articles.title: Why frontline experience and operational research need to come together in the health sector
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The field worker knows which question matters; the researcher brings the systematic approach and methodological rigour needed to investigate it

The road to the village floods for four months every year. While a pregnant woman is put into an ambulance, the hospital has no surgeon on duty. In a semi-permanent ward, a health worker follows a protocol designed for a tertiary hospital that bears little resemblance to the conditions in which they work.

Science, Space & Environment Report: Why frontline experience and operational research need to come together in the health sector. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

articles.title: All-too fallible: On India’s vote against moratorium on death penalty
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Death penalty requires a near-infallible criminal justice system

India’s vote against a proposed global moratorium on the death penalty at the UN is consistent with its position at the forum; it has defended its retention of the penalty as a sovereign decision backed by judicial safeguards, including the “rarest of rare” condition and sessions courts’ sentences requiring a High Court’s confirmation. At the same time, the Supreme Court has increasingly restricted capital punishment and research has failed to find evidence of additional deterrence over life imprisonment . India’s distinction between judicial executions and extrajudicial killings is legally valid but its further claim that due process protects people facing execution is less so. While India last executed convicts in 2020, for the Delhi gang-rape and murder, Parliament expanded the number of capital offences under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita — a form of penal populism that projects the political attractiveness of the state’s response to public outrage, especially in cases of sexual violence, without addressing the poor policing and low conviction rates that actually undermine deterrence . The country had 574 people on death row on December 31, 2025, the highest since 2016, thanks to trial court rulings, challenging claims about judicial safeguards in practice. The report of the 2015 Law Commission headed by Justice A.P. Shah said the death penalty “fails to achieve any constitutionally valid penological goals” and recommended abolishing it for all crimes except terrorism and waging war.

Only a small group of countries worldwide are executing more people. In India, per Project 39A, the Supreme Court released 38 persons from death row in 2016-2025 after they had spent eight years there on average. Some have endured more than two decades. The punishment requires a measure of infallibility that the criminal justice system cannot supply. The safeguards neither deter convictions in cases with flawed evidence, false testimony, and so on nor remedy unequal access to competent legal representation among those facing the penalty. India should formally suspend executions and commission a review of penalty statutes and the treatment of prisoners on death row. Second, it should spare offences that do not involve intentional killing from the penalty. Research suggests meting out excessively harsh punishments for non-fatal crimes could incentivise offenders to escalate their violence, including to kill potential witnesses. The greater goal should be to abolish the practice in law while improving investigative and prosecutorial practices and access to legal aid.

articles.title: Cancel wetland excavation project in eastern Assam grazing grounds, CM urged
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: People from villages in Jorhat district’s Teok region staged a protest in Guwahati, demanding a halt to the ongoing project across 7,598 bighas

Farmers and fishing community members in eastern Assam’s Teok region have urged Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma to scrap an ongoing “anti-people” project in “historic” grazing grounds and natural wetlands. They submitted a memorandum to the Chief Minister after staging a sit-in protest in Guwahati on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) against the project being implemented “in the guise of” a Flood Mitigation by Capacity Augmentation of Wetlands scheme.

The Teok Ban Niskashan Nala Khanan Dabi Samiti, a collective of villagers around the 7,598 bighas (almost 2,512 acres) under excavation, organised the protest. They said the authorities began implementing the project in January without any open public hearings, independent Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), Social Impact Assessment (SIA) or public consent.
Located in Jorhat district, Teok is about 330 km east of Guwahati.

The Hindu had reported on the first resistance in February-March after police served a notice to Debanga Sourav Gogoi, the Samiti’s advisor, for allegedly instigating villagers against the project involving the grazing grounds and the Jelengitup-Ghorachowa, Kenduguri, Garchiga and Kawaimari wetlands.
These wetlands are located within 5 km of the Brahmaputra River’s southern bank.
The Teok Ban Niskashan Nala Khanan Dabi Samiti, a collective of villagers around the 7,598 bighas under excavation, organised the protest on November 18, 2026 | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

Mr. Gogoi said representatives from various progressive organisations, farmer organisations, political parties, students’ unions and civil society participated in Tuesday’s protest to express solidarity with the Samiti.

The other organisations and parties included Rabha Hasong, Asom Nagarik Samaj, Bhumi Adhimar Joutha Sangram Samiti, Silsako Uchchhed Protirudhi Raij, Darabil Go-Soroniya Pothar Suraksha Samiti Raijor Dal, Asom Jatiya Parishad, Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist), and Students’ Federation of India.
Samiti president Ramesh Duara said the organisation listed three demands in the memorandum to the Chief Minister.

The organisation wants the government to stop the excavation work; conduct a transparent and open public hearing in each project area involving independent environmental experts, public representatives, agriculturists, livestock farmers, fishermen and other affected citizens; and ensure legal protection of ancestral rights over the grazing grounds and traditional fishing rights in the targeted wetlands.
