articles.title: CCMB study points to new way of tackling fungal infections
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Fungi can gradually develop resistance to current antifungal drugs, making infections increasingly difficult to treat

Scientists at the CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB), Hyderabad, have identified a promising new strategy to combat fungal infections by preventing disease-causing fungi from becoming invasive, rather than killing them outright.

Most current antifungal drugs work by destroying fungal cells. However, fungi can gradually develop resistance to these medicines, making infections increasingly difficult to treat. A team led by Sriram Varahan at CCMB studied ‘Candida albicans’, a fungus commonly found on human skin and in the body. While generally harmless, it can cause serious infections when it enters the bloodstream or internal organs.

The researchers focused on ‘morphogenesis’, in which the fungus changes from a round-cell form into long, filament-like structures, a transformation allowing the pathogen to evade the body’s immune defences and spread more effectively within tissues.

Earlier studies had shown that glycolysis, the process through which cells metabolise sugar, plays a key role in controlling this shape change. Building on these findings, the team screened a library of small molecules that target glycolysis and identified two compounds capable of blocking the transformation.

Although the fungus continued to grow, it remained in its harmless rounded form suggesting that the compounds could serve as “anti-infective” agents that reduce the fungus’ ability to cause disease without necessarily eliminating it.

The study also identified pyruvate kinase, an enzyme involved in sugar metabolism, as a crucial regulator of fungal morphogenesis. Researchers further found that one of the compounds reduced biofilm formation, a protective layer that helps fungi resist treatment. The compound also increased the effectiveness of widely used antifungal drugs such as fluconazole and amphotericin B.

In a mouse model of systemic Candida infection, treatment with the lead compound significantly improved survival rates, highlighting its potential for future therapeutic development. “Our findings suggest that fungal disease-associated behaviour can be targeted without necessarily stopping fungal growth,” said Dhrumi Shah, first author of the study. “We need further studies to evaluate the compounds effectiveness and safety but by blocking the fungus from becoming invasive, they could complement existing treatments,” said Sriram Varahan.

The findings, published in ACS Infectious Diseases , emerged from a collaboration between CSIR-CCMB and the BRIC-Translational Health Science and Technology Institute, said a press release on Tuesday.

articles.title: Indian national missing after attacks on commercial vessel in Strait of Hormuz
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: MEA said that of the 24 Indian nationals on board MT Tara Gas, 21 have been safely evacuated

An Indian national went missing and two others sustained injuries after their Panama-flagged vessel came under attack in the Strait of Hormuz this week that triggered a strong condemnation from New Delhi.
The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said that of the 24 Indian nationals on board MT Tara Gas, 21 have been safely evacuated.
"We condemn the attack on the Panama-flagged LPG tanker MT Tara Gas in the Strait of Hormuz on 16 November 16," it said in a statement.
India said the targeting of commercial shipping and civilian infrastructure must end.

"Of the 24 Indian nationals on board, 21 have been safely evacuated ashore at Khasab, two injured Indian crew members have been admitted to hospital, while one Indian national remains missing," it added.
The MEA said the Embassy in Oman is closely monitoring the ongoing search and rescue operations in coordination with the Omani authorities.
"We appreciate the timely assistance and support extended by the Government of Oman in the rescue efforts," it said.
New Delhi said the "continuing incidents of attacks on shipping in the region are deeply worrisome and pose a serious threat to the safety of civilian seafarers."

"The targeting of commercial shipping and civilian infrastructure must end, and free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through international waterways, in keeping with international law, must be restored at the earliest," it said in a statement.

India said the targeting of commercial shipping and civilian infrastructure must end.

"Of the 24 Indian nationals on board, 21 have been safely evacuated ashore at Khasab, two injured Indian crew members have been admitted to hospital, while one Indian national remains missing," it added.

The MEA said the Embassy in Oman is closely monitoring the ongoing search and rescue operations in coordination with the Omani authorities.

articles.title: No mandate only women personnel can ‘handle’ women in crowd-control operations, Delhi Police to SC
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The police said it was yet to be determined if “reel-makers can be elevated to the status of journalists or reporters”.
The Delhi Police has told the Supreme Court there is no strict rule that only women police officers must “handle” women in crowd-control operations.

The police was responding to allegations of manhandling women protestors and journalists by male police officers during widespread protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar . The allegations were made in petitions by Network of Women in Media, India, represented by advocate Aarthi Rajan, and others like the Delhi Union of Journalists, Free Speech Collective and the Kerala Union of Working Journalists.
The legal requirement that only women police officers could arrest or carry out searches on women was not a mandate in crowd-control situations, the police submitted in an affidavit.

“With regards to the allegations of manhandling of women journalists, it is respectfully submitted that the requirement of women personnel handling women is not a statutory mandate in the context of crowd-control operations, in the same manner as it is expressly prescribed under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 in relation to searches and arrests,” the police said.

The police said the deployment of women personnel in a crowd-control situation was an “operational consideration” depending on various factors, including the need to maintain propriety, avoid unnecessary confrontation and defuse tensions at a protest site, particularly if there were women participants.
The mere presence or involvement of male police personnel in crowd-control operations during the CJP protest cannot, itself, be construed as misconduct.
There is no legal bar on a male police officer from acting as a first responder. Nor is he stopped from assisting a woman police officer in the discharge of her duties.
“Such decisions have to be taken at the fraction of a second,” the police affidavit said.

The affidavit said an October 11 direction of the apex court to the Delhi Police to not “hinder” journalists, lawyers and other professionals in the discharge of their professional duties did not extend to reel-makers, social media influencers or unruly elements who break the lawful directions of the police at the site of a prohibited assembly.

The police said it “fully respects the role of the press”. However, there were individuals masquerading as journalists by using a camera and a microphone. The protest site, which the police repeatedly said was “illegal”, was replete with ‘content creators’ for YouTube.

The affidavit said though the police had found it difficult to distinguish between journalists and reel-makers, the latter were neither obstructed nor hindered unless they posed a risk to public order and law.
The Delhi Police pointed out that the current laws, guidelines and rules did not consider reel-makers, creative or otherwise, or content-creators as ‘working journalists’.

articles.title: Scrap the Shillong Peak Ropeway Project, say civil society groups
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Rs. 151-crore tourism project could undermine the area’s water catchment area, they argue.

For nearly a fortnight, women from the Laban Pyllun area and other parts of Shillong have been peacefully protesting the ₹151-crore Shillong Peak Ropeway Project proposed near the Lum Shillong water catchment area. The project, which hopes to augment local tourism, could disrupt local water supply to the community as its many springs and streams will be undermined, the protestors claim.

The women, under the aegis of the Joint Action Committee Against the Shillong Ropeway Project and for the Protection of the Lum Shyllong Catchment (JAC) are demanding that the Meghalaya government scrap the project that could imperil the ecology of the area.

articles.title: At Deepavali celebration, Mamdani flags targeting of Hindu temples
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The New York mayor said this year's Deepavali also served as a reminder of the work still needed to build a politics rooted in tolerance and compassion

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani flagged the targeting of Hindu temples in the U.S. in recent months and the growing presence of hate in political campaigns, calling on communities to reject divisive politics and stand together against discrimination.

Speaking at a Deepavali celebration he hosted in New York on Tuesday (November 17), Mr. Mamdani said Hindu temples had been targeted over the past year and alleged that leaders at the highest levels of the U.S. federal government had also targeted Sikhs.
He said hatred that was once confined to the margins of society has increasingly found a place at the centre of political campaigns.
"Whether it is fear-mongering in Washington or Delhi, we hold a shared obligation, as we mark this holiday, to reject any politics that brings darkness into this world," the mayor said.

Addressing those whose identity and belonging had been questioned, Mr. Mamdani said, “To anyone who has been told to go back home, whose belonging has been questioned, let me say unequivocally, you are home.”

The mayor, whose mother is Punjabi-Hindu and father a Gujarati Ugandan Muslim, spoke about growing up with a diverse cultural and religious heritage, saying his family had taught him to appreciate the beauty and wisdom of Hinduism.
"Our shared heritage was never a single language, faith, or affiliation. From an early age, my mother's family taught me how much beauty and wisdom lives in Hinduism,” he said.

Describing Hinduism as a faith with many gods and diverse narratives, Mr. Mamdani referred to its scriptures and the idea that there are multiple paths to truth and that the same light resides in everyone, irrespective of whether they worship at a temple, mosque, gurdwara or do not follow a religion.

"It is a faith of many gods... it's a faith whose oldest scripture teaches us that there are many roads to Satya (truth), and that the same light lives in every one of us, whether we pray in a mandir, a masjid, a gurudwara, or nowhere at all,” he said.
Mr. Mamdani also drew upon the Ramayana and the Mahabharata, saying the epics offered lessons on relationships, family, duty and moral responsibility.

“Ramayana shows us the brother, the wife, the husband, and the friend that we aspire to be. The Mahabharata shows us what families are really like, where even the bravest heroes and wisest gods stumble, and where one's Dharma must come before one's loyalty,” he noted.

Mr. Mamdani said the wisdom of these traditions had resonated beyond religious practices and influenced movements for justice across the world, citing Mahatma Gandhi's Salt March and Martin Luther King Jr's March on Washington.

articles.title: Why did the U.S. lose its measles elimination status? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: What triggered the resurgence of measles in the U.S.? Is vaccine hesitancy putting decades of progress against measles at risk? How is the global measles surge affecting India?

The story so far: After 26 years of holding on to its measles elimination status, the United States lost this distinction. On November 17, 2026, the Pan American Health Organisation (PAHO) revoked the United States’ measles elimination status. This was after over 5400 cases of measles were reported in the U.S. in 2026.

This is the highest annual total since 1989-91, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention(CDC). As per data put out by the Unicef, 96% of cases are in unvaccinated people or those with unknown vaccination status. Children under five account for 18% of cases and those aged 5-19 for 40%.

Global & Diplomatic Brief: Why did the U.S. lose its measles elimination status? | Explained. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and proactive engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

Geopolitical Significance: Strengthening strategic partnerships across the Indo-Pacific, Global South, and multilateral forums such as the UN, G20, BRICS, and SCO remains central to India's foreign policy.

articles.title: Why Ukraine keeps targeting the Kerch Bridge
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Ukraine has targeted the structure several times, latest on November 17, 2026

In 2022, Ukraine bombed the Kerch bridge linking mainland Russia to the Crimean Peninsula, using explosives hidden in a truck. In 2023, naval drones struck the bridge. In 2025, covert Ukrainian operatives planted bombs on its undersea support pillars. But none of these attacks caused major damage to the structure, which Russian President Vladimir Putin described in 2018 as a “miracle”. But earlier this week, two back-to-back Ukrainian attacks, involving drones and missiles, brought down a crucial span of the road bridge and damaged the parallel rail bridge. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy hailed it as an “unprecedented operation”. Russian authorities acknowledged the damage, announcing a suspension of road traffic and restrictions on train services.

The 19-km Kerch bridge , across the Kerch Strait, which connects the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov, is the longest bridge in Europe, built at a cost of $3.6 billion. It was opened in 2018 by Russian President Vladimir Putin, four years after Russia annexed Crimea from Ukraine through a contested referendum. Mr. Putin drove an orange truck across its length and said “a miracle has come true”.

The bridge is important for Russia for symbolic, administrative and operational reasons. When Russia swiftly moved to annex Crimea in 2014 , after a pro-Russian elected government in Kyiv fell amid West-backed anti-regime protests, there was no direct connectivity between the Russian mainland and the peninsula, which hosts Russia’s Black Sea fleet. Mr. Putin immediately ordered the construction of the bridge. But the bridge remained a weak link as Ukraine grew in military strength, backed by the West, in subsequent years.

This 2017 photo shows the newly installed railroad arch of a road-and-rail bridge under construction to connect the Russian mainland with Crimea, at dawn in the Kerch Strait, Crimea. | Photo Credit: Reuters

When Mr. Putin ordered the invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022 (what Russia calls a ‘special military operation’), one of the military objectives, according to experts, was to secure a “land bridge” from southwest Russia to Crimea, where 77% of the local population identified Russian as their native language. Today, Russia has the land bridge extending from northeastern Ukraine through the Donbas and Kherson to Crimea. But the bridge remains a critical logistical supply link for the Russian troops in the south. And for Crimea, which depends on mainland Russia for much of its food, fuel and consumer goods, the bridge is also an economic lifeline.

If Russia sees the bridge as a symbol of pride, Ukraine sees it as a symbol of occupation. Russia also used Crimea as a launchpad to start its 2022 invasion. That’s why Ukrainians have repeatedly targeted the bridge. The context of the latest attack is also significant. The attack came just days ahead of President Putin’s trilateral meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen.

According to Mr. Zelenskyy, Ukraine carried out a seven-stage operation, disabling Russian radars, air defence and electronic warfare systems protecting the bridge, before launching a two-tier attack with missiles and drones. The damage caused to the bridge, according to Ukraine, is a blow to Mr. Putin. Russia built a myth around it as a symbol of Crimea being ‘Russian forever’,” the Ukrainian military said in a statement after the attack.

While the damage caused to the Kerch bridge and the halt in traffic are clearly a setback to Russia, the impact would be less consequential for Moscow than what it would have been in 2022. Before the war, Russia was almost entirely dependent on the bridge to move people, goods and equipment across the Kerch strait. But today, Russia has a land corridor connecting its southeast with the Crimean Peninsula. Russia has also started ferry services across the strait which could offset the impact of any disruption in traffic on the bridge. Yet, the attack shows Ukraine’s growing capability to strike even Russia’s most fortified infrastructure as both sides continue to exchange fire.

articles.title: Donald Trump says U.S. has concluded ‘very big trade deal’ with Philippines

fullParagraphs: We were very happy with that, and we didn’t know that was going to take place, Donald Trump said

U.S. President Donald Trump said on Wednesday ‌(November 18, 2026) that the United States has ​just concluded a “very big ⁠trade deal” with the Philippines, but he did not provide any details, and Manila ‌did not announce any agreement.

“We’ve just consummated a very big ‌trade deal, the biggest trade deal ‌we’ve ⁠ever made so far, ⁠and it is a fair deal for both countries,” Mr. Trump said during a state luncheon ​at the Philippine presidential ‌palace.
“We were very happy with that, and we didn’t know that was going to take place, but ‌it took place very quickly and ​it’s a magnificent deal for both.”
Negotiations on a trade deal ⁠between the two allies were not mentioned in any of the schedules ‌released by either country.

There was no immediate comment from the office of Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. about the deal Mr. Trump was referring to. The Philippines’ ambassador to the United ‌States also did not immediately respond to a ​request for comment.

Mr. Trump said on Tuesday (November 18) that Thailand would eliminate ⁠all tariffs and remove substantial non-tariff barriers ⁠on its imports from the United States as part of a ‌trade deal expected to be finalised in the coming weeks.

fullParagraphs: Bahrain and Kuwait said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) that they had repelled air attacks launched against them following U.S. strikes on an Iranian island, as Gulf nations face retaliatory bombardment in the Middle East war.
The conflict — which began with U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February — has spilled over to Gulf states that host U.S. military facilities.

The Iranian army said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) its drones "targeted Patriot air defence systems and drone and missile launch platforms belonging to the terrorist US military at Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait," in a statement carried by state television IRIB.
Kuwait's military said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) its air defences were "responding to hostile drone threats", urging its public to follow security and safety advice.
While Bahrain said its air defences intercepted attacks from Iran early on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), a day after Tehran's Revolutionary Guards said they attacked a base used by Washington.

The United States and Iran are in a standoff over the vital Strait of Hormuz, with the U.S. military working to escort ships transiting the waterway in defiance of Tehran's attempts to close the waterway.
Iran's official IRNA news agency cited a regional official as saying the United States had hit Qeshm Island in the Hormuz strait without causing serious damage.

U.S. fighter jets "used precision munitions to strike an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) missile launch site on Qeshm Island", an American official told AFP on condition of anonymity, adding that the strike was in response to Iranian "aggression targeting US personnel and assets".
Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) it had intercepted a cruise missile launched by the Iran-backed group toward the Riyadh area.
Explosions boomed across Bahrain's capital on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) as a mobile phone alert warned residents to seek safety.

Bahrain's armed forces said they "confronted, intercepted and destroyed a number of treacherous Iranian aerial attacks today... before they could achieve their objectives", while Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted a U.S.-operated radar system.

"Combat drones belonging to the Revolutionary Guards carried out a precision operation this morning, targeting a radar system operated by US forces at the Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain," the Guards' Sepah news website said.

articles.title: Gilead signs generic licensing deals for experimental Ebola drug
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: A late-stage trial is testing the drug in people at high risk after exposure. The deals are intended to line up manufacturing and supply before trial results and regulatory filings

Gilead Sciences said on Monday it had signed royalty-free deals with three generic drugmakers to make its experimental Ebola prevention drug available in 127 mainly low- and lower-middle-income countries if it succeeds in trials and wins regulatory approvals.

The deals with Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories, Eva Pharma and Ferozsons Laboratories cover obeldesivir, and include all African countries reporting cases in the current Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak. Obeldesivir has shown activity against several Ebola-related viruses in preclinical studies but is not approved for any use in any country.
A late-stage trial is testing the drug in people at high risk after exposure. The deals are intended to line up manufacturing and supply before trial results and regulatory filings.

Gilead is also expanding remdesivir licences to cover Ebola-related diseases if trial results are positive and regulators approve the drug. The company has donated more than 38,000 remdesivir vials to the Democratic Republic of Congo, Uganda and Kenya, including more than 2,000 recently sent to Kenya for investigational treatment and post-exposure prevention.
Remdesivir is not approved to treat or prevent Ebola Bundibugyo disease, and its clinical effectiveness has not been established.

articles.title: As the West hits pause on AI in schools, India rushes in without a debate

articles.title: Voyager 1, one light-day away from earth today, is a marvel of science
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Measurements lying in the shadows of their successors can find new lives in the light of new theories. The Voyager 1 mission’s longevity made that more apparent, allowing successive generations of researchers to find more uses for its data even as it continues to collect new information

Today, the Voyager 1 spacecraft will be one light-day away from the earth. This means a signal travelling at the speed of light will take one full day to go from the earth to Voyager 1, and signals from the spacecraft will similarly take one day to reach receivers on the earth.

This is a tremendous distance — almost 26 billion kilometres. Since February 17, 1998, Voyager 1 has been the farthest any space mission has been from us. And it keeps going at 61,000 km/hr. But even at such breathtaking speed, Voyager 1 is still barely out of the solar system. Each star’s gravitational and magnetic fields extend out for billions of kilometres around them, bending the destinies of multiple worlds to their stellar will.

articles.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth on November 18: What does it mean?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: NASA’s Voyager 1, humanity’s farthest spacecraft, is about to reach one light-day from Earth, more than 16 billion miles away; Know what it means

NASA’s Voyager 1 is set to cross a historic threshold in space exploration as it is about to become humanity’s first object to reach one light-day from Earth. The iconic probe, which has travelled farther from Earth than any other human-made object since its launch in 1977, is expected to cross the landmark on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) at 5:16:07 a.m. EST (3:46:07 p.m. IST), according to NASA.
Infographics: Voyager I’s 49-year journey into the void
Having spent 49 years, two months and 11 days hurtling through the cosmos, Voyager 1 continues to push the boundaries of human space exploration.

One light-day is a staggering measure of distance, rather than a measure of time. It represents the exact space that light, which travels at roughly 186,000 miles (300,000 kilometres) per second, covers in a full 24-hour period.
For Voyager 1, this is equivalent to more than 16 billion miles away from Earth.
When Voyager 1 reaches that incredible milestone on November 18, its radio signals will take precisely 24 hours travelling at the speed of light to reach Earth — in other words, one light-day.

Sunlight takes just over eight minutes to reach Earth, and over four hours and 10 minutes to reach Neptune. From November 18, any radio command sent from NASA’s Deep Space Network to Voyager 1 will take a full 24 hours to arrive, requiring another 24 hours for the spacecraft’s response to return.

Launched on September 2, 1977, Voyager 1 was originally designed for a four-year mission to study Jupiter and Saturn. Its trajectory eventually allowed it to overtake its twin, Voyager 2, which was launched 16 days earlier. According to NASA, Voyager 2 is expected to reach the one-light-day distance from Earth in November 2035.

The two spacecrafts were launched to explore the outer planets, with Voyager 1 taking a trajectory that eventually carried it towards interstellar space. It became the first spacecraft that entered the interstellar space in August 2012 and has continued transmitting information from beyond the solar system. Today, it speeds onward at roughly 38,000 miles per hour.
In 1990, Voyager 1 captured the most distant image of Earth, known as the iconic “Pale Blue Dot,” while venturing farther than any other human-made object beyond Neptune.
NASA said Voyager 1 is currently travelling in the direction of a star known as AC +79 3888, or Gliese 445, located more than 17 light-years from Earth in the constellation Ursa Minor.

Powered by decaying plutonium generators, Voyager 1 loses a small amount of electrical power every year. With this plutonium supply continually depleting, both probes lose about 4 watts of power each year.

articles.title: This 2D rhythm platformer video game is an ode to India’s multiplicities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Suri: The Seventh Note by Tathvamasi Studios is set in a universe controlled by evil music. The game was launched in October

The story of Suri: The Seventh Note, a 2D video game by Bengaluru-based Tathvamasi Studios, is set in a world corrupted by an evil version of music. Everything in this universe moves in tune with that nefarious sonic presence. The protagonist, Ajira, must find a fruit located at the centre of the island to save her mother from certain death. Soon, she realises her actions shall determine the fate of the island itself.

Suri: The Seventh Note is the brainchild of Glen Martin from Kochi, founder of Tathvamasi Studios, who is also the game director of the video. He is joined by Chitrak Srivastava, co-founder and the game’s art director. The game was launched on Playstation Store and Steam, in October for PlayStations and PCs.

Glen, formerly a data scientist, found himself immersed in game-making during the pandemic. He began by making smaller games, with friends from different places joining him on a Discord server to help. “When we started to build the game, it was not meant to be a project. But once we realised its potential, we began to think about what could be unique about this game,” says Glen.
Glen Martin and Chitrak Srivastava | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT

“At that point, I was playing a parry-focused combat game called Sekiro. It’s a very hard game, and I am not good at it. But then I saw a lot of streamers play the game skilfully, without even taking a single hit, and I realised that when the game is played at that level, it has a certain rhythmic quality to it,” he adds. “The sounds of the sword clinking, the jumps and movements, everything felt choreographed.”
This ultimately led him to turn Suri… into a rhythm platformer game.

Suri... is a mix of two different games: rhythm and platformer. Rhythm games are music-themed action games that assess a player’s sense of timing and metre, while platformers are a sub-genre where a main character moves through uneven terrain and suspended platforms.

“There are very few games that I’ve done this before, so our well of references was limited. In Suri..., the world moves to the rhythm. All the things that you would normally interact with in a regular platformer, like traps, obstacles, etc., are all tied to the rhythm in our game. You have to listen to the music to understand when a thing would move up and down or when a leaf would open or close and so on,” explains Glen. “When done well, it feels like dancing through levels.”

In 2024, Suri was one of five games at the inaugural edition of PlayStation’s India Hero Project, an incubator programme from Sony Interactive Entertainment. This ultimately allowed Glen to quit his job and hire more people.
A still from Suri: The Seventh Note | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT

One of the most intriguing aspects about Suri is the world it is set in. “Suri is set in our own version of mythical India. While we are inspired by Indian ethos and culture, we have not tried to mimic it or take things from it directly. We’ve tried to create our own world,” says Glen.

Chitrak says, “We wanted to create something that belongs to those places we grew up in. Usually when you play these games, they mostly have European or Japanese settings. We wanted to find something that we could relate to and have the world explore that side of our culture. That was the north star for us, while we began developing this world.”

articles.title: One in five women in parts of Northeast deficient in vitamin B1: ICMR-NIN study
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Vitamin B1 or Thiamine is an essential micronutrient that supports energy metabolism and healthy nervous system function

Around one in five pregnant and lactating women in Assam’s Barak Valley and adjoining districts of Tripura suffer from suboptimal levels of ‘Thiamine’ (vitamin B1), according to a study by the ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition (ICMR-NIN), Hyderabad, highlighting a continuing public health concern in the region.

The study, ‘Re-Emergence of Thiamine Deficiency Among Pregnant and Lactating Women in Northeast India’, published in the Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences, examined the prevalence of thiamine deficiency and its link to dietary practices in areas where beriberi cases have previously been reported, said a press release on Monday.

Researchers conducted the community-based study during 2023-24 among 1,083 women from 120 villages in Assam’s Barak Valley and neighbouring parts of Tripura. Thiamine status was assessed using biochemical and functional indicators to determine the extent of deficiency.

The findings showed that about 20% of participants had inadequate thiamine levels. Based on blood thiamine measurements, 4.9% were deficient, and 15.2% had marginal levels. A separate functional assessment produced similar results, with 8.5% showing severe deficiency and 12.1% marginal deficiency. Pregnant women were found to be more vulnerable than lactating mothers.

Thiamine is an essential micronutrient that supports energy metabolism and healthy nervous system function. Deficiency can lead to serious health complications, making adequate intake particularly important during pregnancy and breastfeeding.

According to Mahesh Kumar Mummadi, NIN scientist and lead author of the study, dietary assessments revealed that most women consumed rice-based diets with limited diversity. Practices such as consuming stored rice, repeatedly washing rice before cooking, chewing betel nut and drinking salted tea were associated with a higher risk of deficiency.

One in five women in parts of Northeast deficient in vitamin B1: ICMR-NIN study

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports

Vitamin B1 or Thiamine is an essential micronutrient that supports energy metabolism and healthy nervous system function

Around one in five pregnant and lactating women in Assam’s Barak Valley and adjoining districts of Tripura suffer from suboptimal levels of ‘Thiamine’ (vitamin B1), according to a study by the ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition (ICMR-NIN), Hyderabad, highlighting a continuing public health concern in the region.

The study, ‘Re-Emergence of Thiamine Deficiency Among Pregnant and Lactating Women in Northeast India’, published in the Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences, examined the prevalence of thiamine deficiency and its link to dietary practices in areas where beriberi cases have previously been reported, said a press release on Monday.

Researchers conducted the community-based study during 2023-24 among 1,083 women from 120 villages in Assam’s Barak Valley and neighbouring parts of Tripura. Thiamine status was assessed using biochemical and functional indicators to determine the extent of deficiency.

The findings showed that about 20% of participants had inadequate thiamine levels. Based on blood thiamine measurements, 4.9% were deficient, and 15.2% had marginal levels. A separate functional assessment produced similar results, with 8.5% showing severe deficiency and 12.1% marginal deficiency. Pregnant women were found to be more vulnerable than lactating mothers.

Thiamine is an essential micronutrient that supports energy metabolism and healthy nervous system function. Deficiency can lead to serious health complications, making adequate intake particularly important during pregnancy and breastfeeding.

According to Mahesh Kumar Mummadi, NIN scientist and lead author of the study, dietary assessments revealed that most women consumed rice-based diets with limited diversity. Practices such as consuming stored rice, repeatedly washing rice before cooking, chewing betel nut and drinking salted tea were associated with a higher risk of deficiency.

NIN director Bharati Kulkarni said the findings underscore the need to look beyond routinely monitored nutrients in maternal health programmes. She called for greater dietary diversity, regular nutritional surveillance and targeted supplementation in high-risk regions. Researchers also noted that since the study focused on areas with previously reported beriberi clusters, the findings may not be representative of all pregnant and lactating women across India.

She called for greater dietary diversity, regular nutritional surveillance and targeted supplementation in high-risk regions. articles.title: Koppal MP distributes electric three-wheelers to eight persons with disabilities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: MP Rajashekar Hitnal said the vehicles would help the beneficiaries become financially and socially self-reliant by reducing their dependence on petrol-powered transport and the burden of daily fuel expenses.
Eight persons with disabilities were provided with electric three-wheelers under the Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme for 2024-25 and 2025-26 on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

Koppal MP K. Rajashekar Hitnal handed over TVS iQube electric vehicles to the beneficiaries at the District Administration Complex. He interacted with them, handed over the vehicle keys and wished them well.

Speaking to reporters, Mr. Hitnal said the vehicles would help the beneficiaries become financially and socially self-reliant by reducing their dependence on petrol-powered transport and the burden of daily fuel expenses. “A fully charged vehicle could cover a distance of 100 to 115 km. The vehicles would enable the beneficiaries to travel conveniently for work, education and family-related activities,” he said.

District Disabled Persons Welfare Officer Venkatesh Deshpande said eight vehicles had been sanctioned under the scheme for the two financial years. They were purchased through a tender process from Umamaheshwar LLP Motors, Gangavathi, at a cost of ₹1,69,410 each, involving a total expenditure of ₹13,55,280, he said.
Several public representatives, officials and staff of various departments were present.

articles.title: Season’s first ground frost recorded in the Nilgiris
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Temperatures between 5°C and 6°C were recorded in the higher elevations of the district

The first seasonal ground frost was recorded in the Nilgiris on the intervening night of Tuesday (November 17, 2026) and Wednesday (November 18), as temperatures between 5°C and 6°C were recorded in the higher elevations of the district.

While frost usually sets in in late November or early December, the season was extremely delayed in 2025. However, the delay in the onset of ground frost led to colder weather in the early part of that year, with many places, especially Thalakundha, becoming tourist hotspots as the area was blanketed by ground frost.
While frost usually sets in in late November or early December, the season was extremely delayed in 2025 | Photo Credit: M. Sathyamoorthy

According to officials, ground frost was seen early Wednesday morning in the low-lying parts of Ooty town surrounding Ooty lake, as well as in Thalakundha, Khandal, and a few other areas. Temperature gauges recorded lows of anywhere between 5°C and 6°C.

Over the last few years, pictures of the district’s annual ground frost have led to an increase in tourism footfall in the district, with visitors keen to witness this weather phenomenon, which occurs when ground temperatures fall below freezing, causing ice crystals to form from condensed water vapour and creating the illusion of snow carpeting open expanses, particularly grasslands.

Over the last few years, pictures of the district’s annual ground frost have led to an increase in tourism footfall in the district, with visitors keen to witness this weather phenomenon | Photo Credit: M. Sathyamoorthy

The ground-frost season also has ecological implications, with the phenomenon helping to curtail the spread of invasive species into the upper Nilgiris, as many species of invasive flora are unable to tolerate the extreme cold that native and endemic species have evolved to withstand and thrive in.

articles.title: Over 50 students of Keralam school hospitalised after suspected pollution from tar-mixing unit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Panchayat authorities had earlier issued a stop memo against the tar-mixing plant located close to the school in Kollam. However, it resumed operations after obtaining court permission, local residents claimed

Around 50 students of Auxilium ISC School at Kottiyam in Kollam district of Keralam were rushed to a nearby private hospital on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) afternoon after experiencing acute health distress, including severe breathing difficulties, nausea, and vomiting. The sudden medical emergency sparked panic among parents and school authorities, prompting an immediate evacuation of the affected classrooms.

Local residents and parents have strongly alleged that toxic fumes emanating from a tar-mixing unit located in close proximity to the school campus triggered the incident. According to them, thick smoke began drifting into the school premises shortly after the facility resumed operations earlier in the day.

This is not the first time the industrial unit has been linked to health hazards in the area. In a similar incident previously, more than 10 students from the same school were hospitalised with identical symptoms. Following public outcry and protests from parents at the time, the panchayat had issued a formal stop memo, forcing the unit to suspend its operations.

However, tensions flared again on Wednesday morning when the tar-mixing plant reopened after securing a favourable court order. Within hours of the machinery starting up, dozens of children began falling ill.
“We warned the authorities that restarting this unit would put our children’s lives at risk. How can a court order override the basic right of these children to breathe clean air?” a parent asked.

Echoing the sentiment, a local resident demanded permanent closure of the facility. “The panchayat issued a stop memo earlier because the pollution was unbearable. After they restarted the plant this morning, ambulances were rushing our children to the hospital. We will not allow this unit to function here anymore,” he said.
Hospital authorities confirmed that the admitted students are currently under close medical observation and their condition is reported to be stable.

articles.title: Annamalai flays TVK-led govt. over delay in appointing Cauvery technical cell vice-chairman
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The delay in filling such a crucial position raises questions about the government’s administrative efficiency and sense of responsibility, he says

We The Leaders founder K. Annamalai on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) termed as unacceptable the delay in appointing the vice-chairman of the Cauvery Technical Cell-cum-Inter-State Waters Wing by the Tamil Nadu government.

In a post on X, Mr. Annamalai said the resignation of M. Selvaraj, who served as vice-chairman of the Cauvery Technical Cell-cum-Inter-State Waters Wing, was accepted on June 28, 2026. However, the Government Order (G.O.) to fill this post was issued only on October 9, 2026. Even more than a month after the issuance of the G.O., there is no information so far on the appointment of a new vice-chairman.

The delay in filling such a crucial position, which plays a significant role in safeguarding Tamil Nadu’s water rights and dealing with inter-State river water disputes, raises questions about the government’s administrative efficiency and sense of responsibility. This is not an ordinary administrative post but one that involves important technical and legal responsibilities in protecting Tamil Nadu’s water rights, he said.

On the one hand, farmers in the Cauvery delta districts are worried over the lack of adequate water for Samba cultivation. On the other, the Cauvery water-sharing dispute continues, while Karnataka’s proposed Mekedatu dam project remains a challenge to Tamil Nadu’s rights. “At a time when the State is confronted with several such critical issues, the vacancy in the key post of vice-chairman of the Cauvery Technical Cell-cum-Inter-State Waters Wing is nothing but a serious administrative failure,” he said.

Reports have emerged that Tamil Nadu Ministers N. Anand and Aadhav Arjuna are set to meet the Union Minister for Jal Shakti and submit a representation on the Mekedatu dam issue. “Does the TVK government believe that meeting a Union Minister and submitting a representation alone will resolve these issues, without strengthening the State’s own administrative machinery and making timely appointments to key positions?” Mr. Annamalai questioned.

Such administrative delays and lack of accountability by the TVK government in matters of such significance, which concern the livelihoods of farmers and Tamil Nadu’s water rights, are wholly unacceptable, he added.

articles.title: DC inspects public parks in Yadgir, orders anti-encroachment drive and formation of ward committees
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Amid widespread complaints that open public spaces were being encroached upon due to the lack of boundary walls, Mr. Pandve stressed the need for immediate protective measures.

​To curb the encroachment of government land, rejuvenate public parks, and expedite the resolution of civic issues, Yadgir Deputy Commissioner Rahul Pandve has directed the City Municipal Council (CMC) Commissioner to constitute citizen committees across every ward in the city.

​Accompanied by Superintendent of Police Pruthvik Shankar and CMC Commissioner Umesh Chavan, the Deputy Commissioner conducted a spot inspection of several public parks in Gandhi Nagar and Wards 25 and 26 on Monday (November 16) morning to assess their present condition.

articles.title: Andhra’s first semiconductor plant to come up near Visakhapatnam with ₹2,387 crore investment
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The chip assembly and testing unit at Tarluvada is the State’s first project under the India Semiconductor Mission and will create 1,000 jobs

Andhra Pradesh is set to mark its entry into the high-technology semiconductor manufacturing sector with Advanced System In Package Technologies Private Limited establishing an Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test (OSAT) facility at Tarluvada village in Anandapuram mandal of Visakhapatnam district.

Cleared with a total proposed investment of ₹2,387.81 crore across two phases, the facility is projected to generate direct employment for 1,000 people, beginning with an outlay of ₹542.19 crore and 200 jobs in Phase I, followed by ₹1,845.61 crore and 800 jobs in Phase II.

In the global microelectronics value chain, an OSAT unit performs the crucial back-end stages of chip production. It takes fabricated silicon wafers and carries out precision assembly, protective encapsulation and rigorous electrical testing before the finished integrated circuits are deployed in mobile devices, telecommunications gear, consumer electronics and automotive systems.

Approved by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) under the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) on August 20, 2025, the Tarluvada plant holds strategic significance as the first ISM-sanctioned project to be grounded in Andhra Pradesh.

By building domestic capacity in chip packaging and testing, the project addresses a critical link in India’s semiconductor supply chain while anchoring a high-value electronics ecosystem on the east coast.

To expedite the project, the State government has rolled out an extensive package of fiscal, land and infrastructure support under the Andhra Pradesh Semiconductor and Display Fab Policy (4.0), 2024–29. Following clearance by the State Council of Ministers on February 24, 2026, the Information Technology, Electronics and Communications (IT, E&C) Department issued formal orders on February 27, 2026, treating the venture as a “special case” in view of its status as the State’s maiden ISM project.

Under the order, the Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (APIIC) will allot 30 acres of land at Tarluvada at a nominal rate of ₹1 per acre. The State will also extend special incentives of up to 40% of the project cost on a pari passu basis alongside the Government of India’s 50% grant disbursement.

Additionally, APIIC has been entrusted with developing external infrastructure, including approach roads, power and water supply, funded through the IT, E&C Department, while the Revenue, Energy and Municipal Administration and Urban Development departments, along with the Visakhapatnam District Collector, VMRDA and APEPDCL, have been instructed to work in tandem for early execution.
State IT Secretary Katamneni Bhaskar said regulatory hurdles had been cleared at both the State and Central levels to facilitate rapid execution.

“Work has started on the ground. All statutory clearances have been issued proactively by the State government, and the Government of India has also approved all clearances on its end. The company now has to speed up the works on the ground to complete the project on time,” Mr. Bhaskar told The Hindu .

articles.title: U.S. proposes tougher rules for employment-based green cards, longer hiring process
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Proposed changes would extend advertising periods, curb tailoring of jobs to foreign workers, shift to online recruitment, and increase scrutiny of employers’ efforts to hire Americans before sponsoring visas

The U.S. has proposed stricter rules for employment-based green cards for foreign workers to ensure that Americans get priority in recruitment for jobs ranging from physical therapists and nurses to highly skilled professionals.

The Department of Labour on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) proposed a new rule to modernise the labour market test under the Programme Electronic Review Management (PERM) immigrant visa process, the first major revision of the rules in 20 years.
Under the proposed changes, employers would be prohibited from tailoring job opportunities to foreign workers.
The proposed rule would require employers to level the playing field when recruiting workers by using the same channels and methods when advertising jobs.
The proposal seeks to replace traditional print advertisements with online recruitment through employer websites, job portals, social media platforms, job fairs and campus recruitment.

It would also extend the minimum period for advertising vacancies from the existing 30 days to 90 calendar days and require employers to demonstrate that they had made genuine efforts to recruit qualified American workers.
“This proposed rule change will ensure American workers are first in line for high-skilled, high-paying job opportunities over foreign labour,” Secretary of Labour Keith Sonderling said.
The department also proposed to eliminate the administrative exemption that allowed employers to bypass the statutory labour market test for certain occupations.

Under the revised framework, employers recruiting for physical therapists, nurses, and positions requiring exceptional ability in the sciences or arts would have to consider qualified American applicants.

The proposal also seeks to strengthen safeguards for American workers who have been laid off. Employers would be required to continue considering qualified laid-off workers throughout the labour certification and immigrant petition processes.
Comment | The U.S.’s immigration blocks as a self-defeating path
It would bar certain employers who have laid off American workers within the preceding two years from seeking permanent labour certification for the same or similar positions.

articles.title: Deutsche Bank chair backs CEO after reports expose past lapses; Trump calls tax leak ‘illegal’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Reports cite 15 million leaked records reviewed by more than 200 journalists; German Finance Minister calls for authorities to investigate

Deutsche Bank’s chairman backed ​his CEO Christian Sewing on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) after a huge cache of leaked internal records renewed scrutiny ⁠of the German lender’s past dealings with clients including Russian oligarchs, U.S. President Donald Trump and sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

The reports, compiled by a consortium of international journalists and published by outlets including Der Spiegel , the Financial Times , the New York Times and Le ‌Monde , examined Deutsche Bank’s dealings with Mr. Trump, Epstein and Russian oligarchs, including its pursuit of business in Russia before the 2022 invasion of Ukraine.
Deutsche Bank, whose shares fell by as much as 6%, ‌said the matters in the various reports “date back many years”, and that the bank had since strengthened its ‌controls.
Christian Sewing, Chief Executive Officer of Deutsche Bank | Photo Credit: Reuters

“During ⁠my tenure, I haven’t seen a single decision from Christian Sewing that I was not comfortable ⁠with,” Deutsche Bank Chairman Alexander Wynaendts said in an emailed statement. Mr. Sewing has led Germany’s biggest lender since 2018.

The Financial Times reported that Deutsche Bank had inadvertently sent a Trump tax document to another client’s accountant in 2017 when the President was a Deutsche Bank client during his first ​term in office.
Asked in Manila about the ‌error, Mr. Trump said the bank should not have disclosed it. “They shouldn’t have done it. It’s illegal for them to do it,” Mr. Trump said.
Deutsche Bank declined to comment on Mr. Trump’s reaction.

The leaks also showed that Deutsche Bank was ambitious in pursuing business in Russia, including with high-profile oligarchs, right up to the invasion ‌of Ukraine in February 2022, even as some of the bank’s managers voiced concerns over the risks, according ​to the publications.

German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil called on authorities to investigate “and take the necessary action”. Deutsche Bank, he said, needs to explain “with complete transparency” how it has fixed failures and will ⁠prevent new ones.

A member of the European Parliament called on Mr. Sewing to appear before the body to answer questions about the bank’s business practices and control mechanisms. The European Central Bank and the Bank of England’s regulatory arm declined to comment.
The ‌6% share drop was the biggest since April 2025. Shares recouped some losses to trade 3.8% lower by early afternoon.

articles.title: Iran army says it targeted U.S. military base in Kuwait
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The army claimed it had targeted air defence systems, as well as drone and missile launch platforms, according to a statement carried by Iran’s state broadcaster

The Iranian army claimed early on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) it targeted U.S. Ali Al Salem air base in Kuwait with drones, triggering the air defence alerts in the oil-rich Gulf country for the first time in weeks.
The army claimed it had targeted air defence systems, as well as drone and missile launch platforms, according to a statement carried by Iran’s state broadcaster.
U.S. Central Command, which oversees U.S. forces in the West Asia, did not immediately comment.

Earlier on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), Kuwait’s Army said its air defences were intercepting drone attacks but did not immediately report any damage. The country’s Foreign Ministry condemned the repeated Iranian “criminal” attacks and said they threatened Kuwait’s security and stability.

Iran also recently claimed attacks against U.S. military targets in the tiny island kingdom of Bahrain. Iran targeted U.S. facilities and interests in the neighbouring Gulf countries following the U.S. and Israeli strikes against it on Feb 28.

articles.title: Israeli Parliament elects new Knesset Speaker backed by Netanyahu's opponents
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The newly-elected Speaker is Matan Kahana, an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, the party leader currently working to form the next government and replace Mr. Netanyahu
The Israeli Parliament elected a new speaker on Tuesday (November 18, 2026), a key step toward rolling back policies passed by the outgoing government led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The newly-elected Speaker is Matan Kahana, an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, the party leader currently working to form the next government and replace Mr. Netanyahu. Eisenkot's bloc has pledged to undo some of Netanyahu's most contentious policies following Kahana's election.

He was approved as speaker with 66 votes in the 120-member chamber, backed by the Jewish-led opposition parties and by the Arab-led parties. The candidate backed by Netanyahu's bloc, Ofir Katz, received 52 votes following a stormy debate that stretched over seven hours.
"The appointment of Matan Kahana as Knesset speaker is a worthy democratic move that reflects the absolute majority in favour of change," Mr. Eisenkot said ahead of the vote.

The vote took place weeks after October 27 parliamentary elections in which Netanyahu and his allies lost their parliamentary majority. Mr. Eisenkot was subsequently given the task by Israel's president to try to form a new coalition government.

Mr. Eisenkot has up to five more weeks to secure enough alliances to form a coalition. As negotiations continue on the sidelines, his bloc, along with unaffiliated Arab-led parties, can use their majority in the newly-sworn in Knesset to advance their legislative agenda. They introduced several bills last week, including to set term limits on the role of prime minister, to form a government-led inquiry into the Hamas-led Oct 7, 2023, attacks and to reverse laws to limit the powers of the judiciary.
Mr. Kahana gives the opposition bloc a major legislative advantage, according to Assaf Shapira with the Israel Democracy Institute, a Jerusalem think tank.
"It's important because there is not much time, because the speaker of the Knesset can make the legislative process much, much faster or much slower," Shapira said.
Mr. Kahana replaced Amir Ohana, a Netanyahu ally, as speaker.

Mr. Eisenkot and his allies are under pressure to swiftly advance their legislative priorities in the weeks ahead. Currently a member of Eisenkot's Yashar party, Roy Folkman, heads the temporary committee that decides much of the Knesset's work until a government is formed.
If Mr. Eisenkot fails to form a government, the Israeli President could give Netanyahu an opportunity to do so. That would likely give Netanyahu's Likud party control of the committee.

Even though Netanyahu's opponents would still hold a majority, they would "feel that their momentum has gone," Shapira said, and there would be a "real danger that some of the legislation will be delayed."

articles.title: Cyclone Akvan: why is Andhra Pradesh facing a third cyclone in a month?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Warm seas, river water that traps heat near the surface and winds that steer storms towards the coast have made this post-monsoon season unusual, experts say

Andhra Pradesh is currently facing a rare weather phenomenon. Since October 28, the State has already been hit by two back-to-back cyclonic storms, and there is an imminent threat of another one battering the coastal districts in the next two days.

On October 28, the State was battered by very severe cyclonic storm Arnab , which made landfall near Narsapur in West Godavari district. On November 3, it was hit again by severe cyclonic storm Murasu , which made landfall close to Ongole in Prakasam district. Now, cyclonic storm Akvan is likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and make landfall on November 20 between Narsapur and Puri.

Three tropical storms battering the coast within less than a month during the post-monsoon season is a rare scenario. The last times such a thing happened were in 1976, 1987 and 2013. Both 1976 and 1987 were El Niño years, and this year is also categorised as a super El Niño year .

When it comes to tropical cyclones over the Bay of Bengal, there are a number of driving factors, and El Niño is just one of them. Mostly, the formation of storms over the Bay, especially their frequency and intensity, differs slightly from the rest of the world, because the Bay of Bengal is almost a land-locked sea, said S.S.V.S. Ramakrishna, former head of the Department of Oceanography and Meteorology, Andhra University, who has spent over four decades researching the pattern of cyclones over the Bay.
“El Niño typically suppresses the southwest summer monsoon over India, but it has the opposite effect on the Northeast (winter) Monsoon and post-monsoon cyclogenesis in the Bay of Bengal,” he said.

During El Niño years, the northeast monsoon tends to be significantly more active over southern peninsular India. This creates continuous moisture convergence and frequent convective disturbances over the southern Bay, providing a steady assembly line of low-pressure areas.

And sometimes, in rare occurrences, remnants of a Pacific Ocean cyclone cross the Strait of Malacca, re-enter the Bay of Bengal, and intensify into a cyclone. “We had seen this phenomenon during the Odisha Super Cyclone in 1999,” he said.

Mr. Ramakrishna also pointed out that in October and November, the Bay of Bengal consistently retained high sea surface temperatures—over 26.5 degrees Celsius—and anything above 26 is conducive to developing a cyclonic system. This has been aided by the El Niño-modified upper-level wind patterns over the southern Bay of Bengal, which reduce vertical wind shear.

Another key factor that acted as a catalyst is the massive freshwater discharge from rivers like the Ganga, Brahmaputra and Godavari into the Bay of Bengal, which resulted in creating a low-salinity surface layer. This acts as a “barrier layer” that prevents cooler, deeper ocean water from mixing upward, so a passing cyclone (like Arnab or Murasu) does not cool the sea surface enough to stop the next storm from forming days later.

Persistent upper-tropospheric ridges (anticyclonic circulations) over the China–Myanmar region and central India have acted as steering barriers, blocking storms from recurving northeast and forcing them northwestward into the Andhra coast, he said.

articles.title: Kaziranga: 21 elephants died in 22 months, RTI reveals
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Environment activist Dilip Nath sought the information for the January 2025 to October 22, 2026 period

Information obtained under the Right to Information (RTI) Act reveals that 21 elephants died in the Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve during the almost 22-month period between January 2025 and October 22, 2026.
Sonitpur district-based environmental activist Dilip Nath sought the information from the Eastern Assam Wildlife Division, which administers four ranges of Kaziranga National Park, on September 23.

According to the response to his RTI query, 12 elephants died in 2025 and nine died in 2026 (up to October 22). The reply also notes the death of a woman in human-elephant conflict during this period.
However, the wildlife division did not disclose the age or gender of the elephants that died during the 22-month period.

“Poaching or death of rhinos, the flagship species in Kaziranga, has always been a matter of concern. The death of so many elephants in less than two years should also be equally alarming, given the shrinking of space for them,” Mr Nath told The Hindu on Wednesday.

Kaziranga recorded an estimated 1,228 elephants during a 2024 count. According to the seventh Elephant Population Estimation Report released in October 2025, the park’s three wildlife divisions had 1,288 elephants.
Mr Nath said the lack of information on wild elephant deaths on public platforms raises serious questions about transparency in the park’s management.

In addition to their wild counterparts, a few captive elephants engaged by the Forest Department in Kaziranga have died since December 2025. They include Swarnamoyee, a female safari elephant, and Krishna, a female departmental elephant.
Beyond Kaziranga, 626 elephant deaths between 2000 and 2023 were attributed to electrocution, train collisions, poisoning, poaching and retaliatory killings.
A Wildlife Institute of India report said these causes accounted for 52% of the 1,209 elephant deaths recorded over the 23-year period.

articles.title: Kulgam encounter: 25 girls, 2 teachers rescued before final assault on LeT commander Bhat
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Once the civilians were moved to safety, security forces launched the final onslaught.

Anxious moments gripped Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district on Wednesday when it emerged that 25 girls and two teachers were inside a Darul Uloom (educational institute) next to the mosque where top Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) commander Mohammad Lateef Bhat was holed up, just before troops launched the final assault to neutralise him.

Braving heavy fire from the mosque, an officer from the Army's 9 Rashtriya Rifles volunteered and, along with his comrade, entered the adjoining seminary to safely evacuate all 27 civilians, officials said.
Once the civilians were moved to safety, troops of the 9 Rashtriya Rifles and the Special Operations Group (SOG) of the Jammu and Kashmir Police launched the final onslaught.

Tear gas shells were fired into the mosque to smoke the terrorist out while a tight cordon was set up to prevent his escape, as the security forces exercised maximum restraint to ensure the religious structure suffered no damage.
Northern Army Commander Lt. Gen. Pratik Sharma, General Officer Commanding-In-Chief, met troops in South Kashmir after the successful conclusion of the operation.

Giving details of the operation, officials said a search party accompanied by local civilians entered the mosque following specific intelligence inputs and found a room on the top floor locked from the inside.
When asked to come out, the occupant opened fire, confirming the presence of Bhat, who carried a cash reward of Rs 15 lakh on his head, inside the premises.

Senior Army officers in South Kashmir had resolved to ensure that Bhat did not slip through the cordon this time, as he had done on previous occasions. He had escaped an earlier encounter in Shopian on July 8, in which another terrorist, Zakir, was killed.

Following a November 11 attack on a CRPF picket in Kulgam by Bhat and his associate Umar Nasir Dar, which left three personnel injured, security forces launched massive cordon and search operations across Kulgam and the adjoining Shopian and Anantnag districts.
Around 2,000 personnel from the Army, SOG, and CRPF, supported by a Mobile Bunker Command Post (MBCP), were deployed for the grid-based searches.

"Since November 11, cordon and search operations have been underway. In certain areas, it took us nearly three days to complete the searches due to high population density," a senior officer said, adding that while the operations may have caused some inconvenience to the general public, there were no complaints of any excesses.
A school passout and former carpenter, Bhat, who was in his early 20's, went missing on this day in November 2025 before joining LeT and its offshoot, The Resistance Front (TRF).

fullParagraphs: Mr. Goyal met chief executives and senior leaders of Italian companies on November 17, as India and Italy work towards a target of €20 billion in annual bilateral trade by 2029

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal held meetings with chief executive officers and senior leaders of leading Italian companies in Rome, focusing on investment, technology partnerships and joint ventures.

According to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, the meetings took place on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), during the Minister’s official visit to Italy. The talks come as India and Italy take forward their Special Strategic Partnership, and work towards a target of €20 billion in annual bilateral trade by 2029.

Mr. Goyal met several corporate heads, including Walter Tosto S.p.A. Managing Director Luca Tosto, Nordimpianti System S.r.l. Chief Executive Officer Gian Piero Gagliardi and Atitech Chairman Gianni Lettieri. He also held discussions with Magaldi Green Energy Managing Director Letizia Magaldi, and Bracco Imaging S.p.A. Chief Executive Officer Fulvio Renoldi Bracco.
The talks centred on expanding Italian investments in India, facilitating technology transfer, and forming joint ventures with domestic partners.

The Italian firms expressed interest in bringing their technologies to the Indian market, and showed willingness to collaborate with Indian industry across sectors such as manufacturing, aircraft maintenance, thermal energy storage and pharmaceutical ingredients.

Mr. Goyal welcomed the interest shown by the business leaders. He encouraged the firms to partner with Indian industry, specifically pointing to opportunities in India’s infrastructure, aviation and healthcare sectors.
To move the discussions forward, both sides identified several actionable steps, including exploring suitable Indian joint-venture partners and initiating pilot projects.
The participants also noted the need to conduct cost-comparison studies, and to undertake joint studies with Indian institutions to evaluate potential collaborations.

Italy is India’s fourth-largest trading partner in the European Union. Bilateral trade between India and Italy has been growing strongly in the last three years, following the economic recovery after the COVID-19 pandemic. In 2025, bilateral trade registered at €14.25 billion.

India’s exports to Italy reached €8.55 billion, while its imports from Italy were €5.70 billion. The balance of trade remains in India’s favour at €2.84 billion, and has been in India’s favour since 1988.

articles.title: Season’s first ground frost recorded in Nilgiris
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Temperatures between 5°C and 6°C were recorded in the higher elevations of the district

The first seasonal ground frost was recorded in The Nilgiris on the intervening night of Tuesday (November 17, 2026) and Wednesday (November 18), as temperatures between 5°C and 6°C were recorded in the higher elevations of the district.

While frost usually sets in in late November or early December, the season was extremely delayed in 2025. However, the delay in the onset of ground frost led to colder weather in the early part of this year, with many places, especially Thalakundha, becoming tourist hotspots, as the area was blanketed by ground frost.
While frost usually sets in in late November or early December, the season was extremely delayed in 2025 | Photo Credit: M. Sathyamoorthy

According to officials, ground frost was seen early Wednesday morning in the low-lying parts of Ooty town surrounding Ooty lake, as well as in Thalakundha, Khandal, and a few other areas. Temperature gauges recorded lows of anywhere between 5°C and 6°C.

Over the last few years, pictures of the district’s annual ground frost have led to an increase in tourism footfall in the district, with visitors keen to witness this weather phenomenon, which occurs when ground temperatures fall below freezing, causing ice crystals to form from condensed water vapour and creating the illusion of snow carpeting open expanses, particularly grasslands.

Over the last few years, pictures of the district’s annual ground frost have led to an increase in tourism footfall in the district, with visitors keen to witness this weather phenomenon | Photo Credit: M. Sathyamoorthy

The ground-frost season also has ecological implications, with the phenomenon helping to curtail the spread of invasive species into the upper Nilgiris, as many species of invasive flora are unable to tolerate the extreme cold that native and endemic species have evolved to withstand and thrive in.

#Ooty town in The #Nilgiris received this year's first ground frost on Wednesday, with the minimum temperature dipping to 5.9 °C at Government Botanical Garden. 📹&📸: M. Sathyamoorthy (@sathyooty) / The Hindu https://t.co/mn43UCd6vK

articles.title: SC notice to Lokpal on plea against HC verdict saying hearing not needed before show-cause notice
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Delhi High Court, on April 15, had dismissed a petition filed by public servant Chinmoyjit Sen, who had challenged a Lokpal order dated February 25 and a subsequent show-cause notice

The Supreme Court on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) sought a response from the Lokpal of India on a plea challenging a Delhi High Court verdict which held that the anti-corruption ombudsman was not required to provide a public servant an opportunity of hearing before issuing a show-cause notice with regard to an investigation.

The Delhi High Court, on April 15, had dismissed a petition filed by public servant Chinmoyjit Sen, who had challenged a Lokpal order dated February 25 and a subsequent show-cause notice issued on February 27 in connection with a complaint.

Observing that the right to be heard arises before any final action is taken under Section 20(3) of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, the high court had held that the Lokpal was not required to provide a public servant an opportunity of hearing before issuing a show-cause notice.

Section 20(3) of the Act requires a Lokpal bench of at least three members to review preliminary inquiry reports under Section 20(2), hear the public servant, decide if a prima facie case exists and choose one or more actions.
The Lokpal probes allegations of corruption under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 against specified public servants, politicians and certain institutions.
A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana took note of the submissions of Sen's lawyer and issued the notice to the ombudsman.
The bench, however, refused to stay the proceedings before the Lokpal against Sen and said that the matter would be taken up after a week.
The proceedings originated from a preliminary inquiry conducted by the CBI on the directions of the Lokpal.
The CBI submitted its preliminary inquiry report on January 27, following which the Lokpal examined the allegations and found certain of them against Sen to be prima facie substantiated.
The Lokpal subsequently issued a show-cause notice to the petitioner, calling upon him to respond to the two allegations and providing an opportunity of hearing under Section 20(3) of the Act.
Challenging the order and notice, Sen told the high court that the Lokpal had passed the February 25 order without giving him an opportunity of hearing.
It was further said that the Lokpal had already formed an opinion on the allegations, rendering the subsequent show-cause notice and hearing an empty formality.
